series.title: Bill Johnson 講道
series.blurb: 雷丁伯特利教會主任牧師的主日講道，真實語速、口語與幽默，一段 3–6 分鐘。

lines.en: This is Adam and this is Eve, who were the first people on earth.
lines.zh: 這是亞當，這是夏娃，他們是世上最早的人。

lines.en: They lived in the Garden of Eden, which was a beautiful place that had everything they needed.
lines.zh: 他們住在伊甸園，那是一個美麗的地方，凡他們所需要的都有。

lines.en: Adam and Eve took care of the animals and could eat from any of the trees in the garden except for one.
lines.zh: 亞當和夏娃照管動物，園中各樣樹上的果子他們都可以吃，只有一棵除外。

lines.en: This was the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, and God told them not to eat from this tree.
lines.zh: 那就是分別善惡的樹，神吩咐他們不可吃這棵樹的果子。

lines.en: There were lots of animals in the garden, but the serpent was the most clever of all the wild animals God had made.
lines.zh: 園中有許多動物，但在神所造的一切野獸中，蛇最狡猾。

lines.en: One day he asked the woman, "Did God really say you must not eat the fruit from any of these trees in the garden?"
lines.zh: 有一天，蛇問女人：「神豈是真說，不許你們吃園中所有樹上的果子嗎？」

lines.en: Eve said that they were able to eat from all of the fruit trees except the fruit from the tree in the middle of the garden.
lines.zh: 夏娃說，園中所有果樹的果子他們都可以吃，只有園子當中那棵樹的果子不行。

lines.en: "For God said, 'You must not eat or even touch it. If you do, you will die.'"
lines.zh: 「因為神曾說：『你們不可吃，也不可摸，免得你們死。』」

lines.en: "You won't die," said the serpent.
lines.zh: 蛇說：「你們不一定死。」

lines.en: "God knows that as soon as you eat it, you will be like God, knowing both good and evil."
lines.zh: 「因為神知道，你們吃的日子眼睛就明亮了，你們便如神能知道善惡。」

lines.en: The woman was convinced.
lines.zh: 女人被說服了。

lines.en: She saw that the tree was beautiful and its fruit looked delicious, and she wanted the wisdom it would give her.
lines.zh: 她見那棵樹很美，果子看起來好吃，又想得著它能帶來的智慧。

lines.en: So she took some of the fruit and ate it.
lines.zh: 她就摘下果子吃了。

lines.en: Then she gave some to Adam, and he ate it too.
lines.zh: 又給了亞當，他也吃了。

lines.en: At that moment their eyes were opened, and they suddenly realized they weren't wearing clothes and were embarrassed.
lines.zh: 那一刻他們的眼睛就明亮了，忽然發現自己沒穿衣服，覺得很羞愧。

lines.en: So they sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves.
lines.zh: 於是他們用無花果樹的葉子編成裙子遮身。

lines.en: When the cool evening breezes were blowing, Adam and Eve heard God walking about in the garden.
lines.zh: 傍晚涼風吹起時，亞當和夏娃聽見神在園中行走的聲音。

lines.en: So they hid from God among the trees.
lines.zh: 他們就藏在園裡的樹木中，躲避神。

lines.en: Then God called to Adam, "Where are you?"
lines.zh: 神呼喚亞當說：「你在哪裡？」

lines.en: Adam said, "I heard you walking in the garden, so I hid. I was afraid because I was naked."
lines.zh: 亞當說：「我在園中聽見你的聲音，我就藏了。我害怕，因為我赤身露體。」

lines.en: "Who told you that you were naked?" God asked.
lines.zh: 神問：「誰告訴你赤身露體呢？」

lines.en: "Did you eat from the tree I told you not to eat from?"
lines.zh: 「莫非你吃了我吩咐你不可吃的那樹上的果子嗎？」

lines.en: Adam said, "It was the woman you gave me who gave me the fruit, and I ate it."
lines.zh: 亞當說：「你所賜給我、與我同居的女人，她把那樹上的果子給我，我就吃了。」

lines.en: Then God asked Eve, "What have you done?"
lines.zh: 神就問夏娃：「你做的是甚麼事呢？」

lines.en: "The serpent tricked me," she replied. "That's why I ate it."
lines.zh: 她回答：「那蛇引誘我，我就吃了。」

lines.en: Then God punished the serpent by making it so he would crawl on his belly from then on.
lines.zh: 神就懲罰那蛇，使牠從此用肚子行走。

lines.en: He told Eve that she would have great pain in her life.
lines.zh: 祂告訴夏娃，她一生將受許多苦楚。

lines.en: Then God said to Adam that because he listened to Eve and did not obey what God had told him to do, his life would be very difficult.
lines.zh: 神又對亞當說，因他聽了夏娃的話，沒有遵守神的吩咐，他的一生將十分艱難。

lines.en: He would have to work hard to get food to eat.
lines.zh: 他必須辛苦勞碌才得糊口。

lines.en: God said, "For you were made from dust, and to dust you will return."
lines.zh: 神說：「你本是塵土，仍要歸於塵土。」

lines.en: Then God made them clothing from the animals.
lines.zh: 神用動物的皮給他們做衣服。

lines.en: But God knew that Adam and Eve could no longer live in the garden because of their sin.
lines.zh: 但神知道，亞當和夏娃因為犯了罪，不能再住在園子裡。

lines.en: So he sent them away and closed up the garden.
lines.zh: 於是祂打發他們離開，把園子關閉了。

lines.en: Adam and Eve had two sons named Cain and Abel.
lines.zh: 亞當和夏娃有兩個兒子，名叫該隱和亞伯。

lines.en: When Cain and Abel grew up, Cain became a farmer, while Abel became a shepherd.
lines.zh: 當該隱和亞伯長大後，該隱成了一個農夫，而亞伯成了一個牧羊人。

lines.en: Come on, sheep.
lines.zh: 來吧，羊群。

lines.en: When it was time for the harvest, Cain and Abel both brought gifts to God.
lines.zh: 到了收割的時候，該隱和亞伯都帶了禮物獻給神。

lines.en: Cain gathered some of the things he had grown and gave them to God.
lines.zh: 該隱收集了一些他種植的農作物，把它們獻給神。

lines.en: Here you go.
lines.zh: 給你。

lines.en: God wasn't pleased with Cain and his offering, and this made Cain upset.
lines.zh: 神不喜悅該隱和他的供物，這讓該隱很不高興。

lines.en: God asked, "Why are you so angry? Do what is right, and then you will be accepted."
lines.zh: 神問：「你為什麼這樣生氣呢？你若行得好，就必蒙悅納。」

lines.en: God warned Cain about sin.
lines.zh: 神警告該隱要注意罪。

lines.en: God told Cain to be careful not to let sin control him, but instead to take control of sin.
lines.zh: 神告訴該隱要小心，不要讓罪控制他，而是要去制伏罪。

lines.en: Abel also gave a gift to God.
lines.zh: 亞伯也帶了禮物獻給神。

lines.en: Here you go.
lines.zh: 給你。

lines.en: Abel gave God the best part of his firstborn sheep from his flock.
lines.zh: 亞伯將他羊群中頭生的羊，把最好的部分獻給神。

lines.en: God was very pleased with Abel and his offering because he had given the best of what he had.
lines.zh: 神非常喜悅亞伯和他的供物，因為他獻上了自己最好的。

lines.en: Now at this time, Noah pleased God and was the only righteous man living on earth.
lines.zh: 那時，挪亞蒙神喜悅，是地上唯一的義人。

lines.en: He had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
lines.zh: 他有三個兒子：閃、含、雅弗。

lines.en: The earth had become corrupt and was filled with violence.
lines.zh: 世界敗壞了，地上滿了強暴。

lines.en: So God said to Noah, "I have decided to destroy all living creatures, for they have filled the earth with violence."
lines.zh: 神就對挪亞說：「我決定要毀滅一切活物，因為地上滿了他們的強暴。」

lines.en: "Yes, I will wipe them all out with the earth."
lines.zh: 「我要把他們和地一併毀滅。」

lines.en: He instructed Noah, "Build a large boat from cypress wood and waterproof it with tar inside and out."
lines.zh: 祂吩咐挪亞：「你要用歌斐木造一艘大船，裡外抹上松香（瀝青），使它不漏水。」

lines.en: "Then construct decks and stalls throughout its interior."
lines.zh: 「再在裡面建造甲板和一間一間的隔間。」

lines.en: "Make the boat 450 feet long, 75 feet wide, and 45 feet high."
lines.zh: 「船要長 450 呎、寬 75 呎、高 45 呎。」

lines.en: "Leave an 18-inch opening below the roof all the way around the boat."
lines.zh: 「在船頂下方四周留一道 18 吋的透光口。」

lines.en: "Put the door on the side, and build three decks inside the boat: lower, middle, and upper."
lines.zh: 「門要開在旁邊，船內要分上、中、下三層。」

lines.en: "Look," said the Lord, "I am about to cover the earth with a flood that will destroy every living thing that breathes."
lines.zh: 耶和華說：「看哪，我要使洪水氾濫在地上，毀滅一切有氣息的活物。」

lines.en: "But I will confirm my covenant with you."
lines.zh: 「我卻要與你立約。」

lines.en: "So enter the boat, you and your wife and your sons and their wives."
lines.zh: 「你同你的妻，與兒子兒婦，都要進入方舟。」

lines.en: "Bring a pair of every kind of animal, and be sure to take on board enough food for your family and for all the animals."
lines.zh: 「每一種動物都要帶一對，也要帶足夠的食物給你的家人和所有動物。」

lines.en: Noah obeyed God and built the ark precisely as God had instructed.
lines.zh: 挪亞順服神，完全照神的吩咐建造了方舟。

lines.en: The Lord said to Noah, "Go into the boat with all your family, for among all the people of the earth, I can see that you alone are good."
lines.zh: 耶和華對挪亞說：「你和你的全家都要進入方舟，因為在這世代中，我見你在我面前是義人。」

lines.en: "Take with you the animals I approve."
lines.zh: 「把我所認可的動物帶進去。」

lines.en: "Seven days from now I will make the rains pour down on the earth."
lines.zh: 「再過七天，我要降雨在地上。」

lines.en: "It will rain for forty days and forty nights, until I have wiped from the earth all the living things I have created."
lines.zh: 「四十晝夜，把我所造的各種活物都從地上除滅。」

lines.en: At this time, Noah was six hundred years old.
lines.zh: 那時挪亞六百歲。

lines.en: So Noah entered the boat with his wife and his sons and their wives.
lines.zh: 挪亞就同他的妻和兒子兒婦都進入方舟。

lines.en: Two by two, one pair of every kind of animal came into the boat, representing every living thing that breathes.
lines.zh: 各樣的動物一對一對地進入方舟，代表一切有氣息的活物。

lines.en: Then the Lord closed the door behind them.
lines.zh: 耶和華就把他們關在方舟裡。

lines.en: For forty days the flood waters grew deeper, covering the ground and lifting the boat high above the earth.
lines.zh: 洪水氾濫四十天，水勢越漲越深，淹沒地面，把方舟高高托起。

lines.en: The only people who survived were Noah and those with him in the boat.
lines.zh: 只留下挪亞和那些與他同在方舟裡的人。

lines.en: When the time came, God sent a wind and the rain stopped.
lines.zh: 時候到了，神叫風吹地，雨就止住了。

lines.en: Noah opened a window and released a raven.
lines.zh: 挪亞開了窗戶，放出一隻烏鴉。

lines.en: The bird flew back and forth until the flood waters on the earth had dried up.
lines.zh: 那烏鴉飛來飛去，直到地上的水都乾了。

lines.en: He also released a dove to see if it could find dry ground.
lines.zh: 他又放出一隻鴿子，要看看地上是否有乾地。

lines.en: Noah waited, and the dove returned.
lines.zh: 挪亞等候，鴿子回來了。

lines.en: He tried again, and the dove returned to him, this time with a fresh olive leaf in its beak.
lines.zh: 他再試一次，鴿子又回到他那裡，這次嘴裡叼著一片新擰下來的橄欖葉。

lines.en: Noah released the dove again. This time it did not come back.
lines.zh: 挪亞又放出鴿子，這次牠不再回來了。

lines.en: When the earth was dry, God said to Noah, "Leave the boat, all of you."
lines.zh: 地都乾了，神對挪亞說：「你們都出方舟吧。」

lines.en: "Release all the animals so they can be fruitful and multiply throughout the earth."
lines.zh: 「把所有動物都放出來，叫牠們在地上多多滋生，大大興旺。」

lines.en: So Noah, his family, and all the animals followed God's instructions and came out of the ark.
lines.zh: 於是挪亞、他的家人和所有動物都照神的吩咐出了方舟。

lines.en: Noah built an altar to worship the Lord, and this pleased the Lord.
lines.zh: 挪亞為耶和華築了一座壇敬拜祂，耶和華就喜悅。

lines.en: God blessed Noah and his sons and told them, "Be fruitful and multiply. Fill the earth."
lines.zh: 神賜福給挪亞和他的兒子，對他們說：「你們要生養眾多，遍滿了地。」

lines.en: Then God said, "I hereby confirm my covenant with you. Never again will a flood destroy the earth."
lines.zh: 神說：「我與你們立約，凡有血肉的，不再被洪水滅絕，也不再有洪水毀壞地了。」

lines.en: "I am giving you a sign of my covenant by placing my rainbow in the clouds."
lines.zh: 「我把虹放在雲彩中，這就是我立約的記號。」

lines.en: "When I see the rainbow in the clouds, I will remember the eternal covenant between God and every living creature on earth."
lines.zh: 「虹必現在雲彩中，我看見，就要記念我與地上各樣有血肉的活物所立的永約。」

lessons.title: God's Promises for Abraham and Sarah
lessons.titleZh: 神給亞伯拉罕與撒拉的應許

lines.en: God's promises for Abraham and Sarah.
lines.zh: 神給亞伯拉罕與撒拉的應許。

lines.en: This is Abram, and he was married to Sarai.
lines.zh: 這是亞伯蘭，他娶了撒萊為妻。

lines.en: When they lived in Canaan, God told Abram he would give him all the land he could see, and that Abram would have as many children as there are stars in the sky.
lines.zh: 他們住在迦南時，神告訴亞伯蘭，凡他所看見的地都要賜給他，他的子孫也要多如天上的星。

lines.en: God said he would bless Abram's family, and they would be a blessing to all people.
lines.zh: 神說祂要賜福給亞伯蘭的家，他們也要叫萬民得福。

lines.en: Many years passed, and Abram and Sarai were very old and still had no children.
lines.zh: 過了許多年，亞伯蘭和撒萊年紀老邁，仍然沒有孩子。

lines.en: God appeared to Abram again and told him his name would now be Abraham, which means father of many nations.
lines.zh: 神再次向亞伯蘭顯現，告訴他從今以後要叫亞伯拉罕，意思是「多國之父」。

lines.en: God also changed Sarai's name to Sarah, and promised to bless Sarah with a son.
lines.zh: 神也把撒萊的名字改為撒拉，應許要賜福撒拉，使她生一個兒子。

lines.en: One day, Abraham was sitting at the entrance to his tent during the hottest part of the day.
lines.zh: 有一天，正午最熱的時候，亞伯拉罕坐在帳棚門口。

lines.en: When the Lord appeared to him, Abraham saw three men standing nearby, and he went to welcome them.
lines.zh: 耶和華向他顯現，亞伯拉罕看見有三個人站在附近，就上前迎接他們。

lines.en: He asked them to stay with him for a while to rest and eat.
lines.zh: 他請他們留下來休息一會兒，吃點東西。

lines.en: The men agreed.
lines.zh: 那三個人答應了。

lines.en: So Abraham had Sarah and his servant prepare food for the men.
lines.zh: 亞伯拉罕就叫撒拉和僕人為他們預備食物。

lines.en: When the food was ready, Abraham took the food and served it.
lines.zh: 食物預備好了，亞伯拉罕就端去招待他們。

lines.en: The men asked him, "Where is your wife, Sarah?"
lines.zh: 他們問他：「你妻子撒拉在哪裡？」

lines.en: Abraham said, "Over there in the tent."
lines.zh: 亞伯拉罕說：「在帳棚裡。」

lines.en: Then one of them said, "I will return to you about this time next year. Your wife Sarah will have a son."
lines.zh: 其中一位說：「明年這時候我必要回到你這裡，你的妻子撒拉必生一個兒子。」

lines.en: Sarah was listening to this from the tent.
lines.zh: 撒拉在帳棚裡聽見了這話。

lines.en: She laughed to herself, because she thought it was funny to think that she and Abraham could have a child in their old age.
lines.zh: 她心裡暗笑，覺得她和亞伯拉罕這麼老了還能生孩子，實在好笑。

lines.en: Then the Lord said to Abraham, "Why did Sarah laugh? Is anything too hard for me?"
lines.zh: 耶和華對亞伯拉罕說：「撒拉為甚麼笑？耶和華豈有難成的事嗎？」

lines.en: Sarah was afraid, so she lied and said, "I didn't laugh."
lines.zh: 撒拉害怕，就說謊：「我沒有笑。」

lines.en: But the Lord said, "Yes, you laughed."
lines.zh: 耶和華說：「不然，你實在笑了。」

lines.en: A year later, Sarah did have a son.
lines.zh: 一年後，撒拉果然生了一個兒子。

lines.en: They named him Isaac.
lines.zh: 他們給他起名叫以撒。

lines.en: God's promises came true for Abraham and Sarah.
lines.zh: 神給亞伯拉罕和撒拉的應許都實現了。

lines.en: Abraham became the father of many nations.
lines.zh: 亞伯拉罕成了多國之父。

lines.en: And from his child came children, and from their children, more children, until Abraham's descendants were truly more than the stars in the sky, just as the Lord had promised.
lines.zh: 從他的孩子生出孩子，孩子又生孩子，直到亞伯拉罕的後裔真的比天上的星還多，正如耶和華所應許的。

lines.en: This is Jacob, who was later called Israel.
lines.zh: 這是雅各，他後來被稱為以色列。

lines.en: Jacob was the father of twelve sons, who became the twelve tribes of Israel.
lines.zh: 雅各有十二個兒子，他們成為以色列的十二支派。

lines.en: Jacob had a twin brother named Esau.
lines.zh: 雅各有個雙胞胎哥哥，名叫以掃。

lines.en: Even when Jacob and Esau were in their mother's belly, they fought.
lines.zh: 雅各和以掃還在母腹裡的時候，就彼此相爭。

lines.en: As the boys grew up, Esau liked to be outside and to hunt, while Jacob was quiet and liked to stay home.
lines.zh: 兩個孩子長大了，以掃喜歡在外面打獵，雅各則很安靜，喜歡待在家裡。

lines.en: Their father Isaac loved Esau because he liked eating what Esau hunted, but Rebekah, their mother, loved Jacob.
lines.zh: 父親以撒愛以掃，因為他喜歡吃以掃打來的野味；母親利百加卻愛雅各。

lines.en: Esau had a birthright, which means he would get special things and privileges because he was the firstborn.
lines.zh: 以掃有長子的名分，意思是他因為是頭生的，可以得到特別的東西和權利。

lines.en: One day, Jacob was making a stew, and Esau came home very hungry and asked for some.
lines.zh: 有一天，雅各在熬湯，以掃餓著肚子回家，向他要湯喝。

lines.en: Jacob said he would trade Esau some stew for his birthright.
lines.zh: 雅各說，要用湯換以掃長子的名分。

lines.en: Esau agreed, and Jacob was given Esau's birthright.
lines.zh: 以掃答應了，雅各就得了以掃長子的名分。

lines.en: Later on, Isaac, their father, was getting very old, and he wanted to bless his son Esau.
lines.zh: 後來，父親以撒年紀老邁，想要祝福兒子以掃。

lines.en: Isaac's blessing was very important, and Rebekah wanted Jacob to have the blessing instead of Esau.
lines.zh: 以撒的祝福非常重要，利百加想讓雅各、而不是以掃得到這個祝福。

lines.en: So Rebekah told Jacob to pretend to be Esau and go to his father for the blessing.
lines.zh: 利百加就叫雅各假扮成以掃，到父親那裡去領受祝福。

lines.en: Isaac was turning blind, so he believed that Jacob was Esau, and he blessed him.
lines.zh: 以撒眼睛昏花，以為雅各就是以掃，就給他祝福了。

lines.en: Esau came to his father to get his blessing, but Isaac had already given it to Jacob.
lines.zh: 以掃來向父親求祝福，但以撒已經把祝福給了雅各。

lines.en: All of this made Esau hate his brother Jacob.
lines.zh: 這一切使以掃恨他的弟弟雅各。

lines.en: Esau made plans to kill his brother.
lines.zh: 以掃打算殺掉他的弟弟。

lines.en: Rebekah heard of this and had Isaac send Jacob away to live with her family.
lines.zh: 利百加聽說了，就讓以撒打發雅各到她娘家去住。

lines.en: For many years Jacob lived with his uncle and worked in the field, taking care of his flock.
lines.zh: 雅各在舅舅那裡住了許多年，在田間工作，照顧羊群。

lines.en: He started a family and gained many servants, cattle, donkeys, sheep, and goats.
lines.zh: 他成了家，又得了許多僕婢、牛、驢、綿羊和山羊。

lines.en: God told Jacob to leave his uncle's land and go back to the land of his father.
lines.zh: 神吩咐雅各離開舅舅的地，回到他父親之地去。

lines.en: So Jacob took his family and everything he owned and traveled back home.
lines.zh: 雅各就帶著家人和一切所有的，啟程回家。

lines.en: Jacob knew that his brother would be there, though.
lines.zh: 可是雅各知道哥哥會在那裡。

lines.en: So he sent messengers ahead and heard that Esau had an army of four hundred men with him.
lines.zh: 他就先打發使者去，聽說以掃帶著四百人的軍隊。

lines.en: Jacob prayed to God and asked him to rescue him from Esau.
lines.zh: 雅各向神禱告，求祂救他脫離以掃的手。

lines.en: Then he sent gifts ahead of him for his brother.
lines.zh: 他又先送禮物給哥哥。

lines.en: That night Jacob was alone in his camp, for he had sent his family and everything he had ahead of him.
lines.zh: 那夜雅各獨自留在營裡，因為他已經讓家人和所有的一切先過去了。

lines.en: But a man came and wrestled with him until dawn.
lines.zh: 有一個人來和他摔跤，直到黎明。

lines.en: The man saw that he wouldn't win, so he touched Jacob's hip and said, "Let me go."
lines.zh: 那人見自己勝不過他，就摸了雅各的大腿窩，說：「讓我走吧。」

lines.en: But Jacob said, "I will not let you go unless you bless me."
lines.zh: 雅各說：「你不給我祝福，我就不讓你走。」

lines.en: Then the man gave Jacob a new name.
lines.zh: 那人就給雅各一個新名字。

lines.en: He said, "From now on you will be called Israel, because you have fought with God and men and have won."
lines.zh: 他說：「從今以後你要叫以色列，因為你與神與人較力，都得了勝。」

lines.en: The man blessed Jacob.
lines.zh: 那人就給雅各祝福。

lines.en: Jacob left that place, but he had a limp because of the injury to his hip.
lines.zh: 雅各離開那裡，但因為大腿受了傷，走路一瘸一拐。

lines.en: Then Jacob looked up and saw his brother Esau coming with his four hundred men.
lines.zh: 雅各舉目一看，見哥哥以掃帶著四百人來了。

lines.en: Jacob went ahead of his family and bowed to his brother.
lines.zh: 雅各走在家人前面，向哥哥下拜。

lines.en: Esau ran to meet Jacob and hugged him. They both wept.
lines.zh: 以掃跑來迎接雅各，抱住他，兩人都哭了。

lines.en: Jacob introduced Esau to his family and gave him a gift, even though Esau said he had enough.
lines.zh: 雅各把家人介紹給以掃，又送他禮物，雖然以掃說他已經夠了。

lines.en: After everything Jacob and Esau had been through, the brothers made peace with each other.
lines.zh: 經歷了這一切之後，兄弟倆彼此和好了。

lines.en: And Jacob went on to be the father of the great nation of Israel.
lines.zh: 雅各後來成為以色列這個大國的祖先。

lines.en: This is Joseph.
lines.zh: 這是約瑟。

lines.en: Joseph was the son of Israel, also called Jacob, and Rachel.
lines.zh: 約瑟是以色列（也叫雅各）和拉結的兒子。

lines.en: Israel loved Joseph more than all his other sons.
lines.zh: 以色列愛約瑟勝過愛他的其他所有兒子。

lines.en: In fact, he made Joseph a coat of many colors to show him how much he loved him.
lines.zh: 事實上，他為約瑟做了一件彩衣，以表達他有多麼愛他。

lines.en: When Joseph's brothers saw this, they hated Joseph.
lines.zh: 當約瑟的哥哥們看到這個時，他們就恨約瑟。

lines.en: One night, Joseph had a dream.
lines.zh: 有一天晚上，約瑟做了一個夢。

lines.en: Joseph told his brothers, "Listen to the dream I had."
lines.zh: 約瑟對他的哥哥們說：「聽聽我做的這個夢。」

lines.en: "We were tying up bundles of grain out in the field."
lines.zh: 「我們在田間捆麥捆。」

lines.en: "Suddenly, my bundle stood up straight."
lines.zh: 「突然間，我的麥捆站直了。」

lines.en: "Your bundles gathered around my bundle and bowed down to it."
lines.zh: 「你們的麥捆圍著我的麥捆，向它下拜。」

lines.en: This made his brothers hate Joseph even more, and they said, "Will you really rule over us?"
lines.zh: 這使得他的哥哥們更加恨約瑟，他們說：「難道你真的要統治我們嗎？」

lines.en: Then Joseph had another dream, and he told his brothers and his father, "I had another dream."
lines.zh: 後來約瑟又做了一個夢，他告訴他的哥哥們和父親說：「我又做了一個夢。」

lines.en: "This time, the sun and moon and 11 stars were bowing down to me."
lines.zh: 「這一次，太陽、月亮和十一顆星都在向我下拜。」

lines.en: This time, Israel heard the dream and rebuked Joseph, saying, "Will we really come and bow down to the ground in front of you?"
lines.zh: 這一次，以色列聽見了這個夢就責備約瑟說：「我們難道真的要來俯伏在地向你下拜嗎？」

lines.en: The brothers were jealous of Joseph.
lines.zh: 哥哥們都嫉妒約瑟。

lines.en: Israel, however, decided to think about what Joseph had said.
lines.zh: 然而，以色列決定好好思考約瑟所說的話。

lines.en: One day, Joseph's brothers were working when they saw Joseph coming to meet them.
lines.zh: 有一天，約瑟的哥哥們正在工作，這時他們看到約瑟來找他們。

lines.en: One of his brothers said, "Here comes that dreamer."
lines.zh: 他的其中一個哥哥說：「那個做夢的來了。」

lines.en: "Come, let's kill him, then we'll see whether his dreams will come true."
lines.zh: 「來吧，我們把他殺了，然後看看他的夢會不會成真。」

lines.en: Joseph's brother Reuben wanted to save Joseph, so he said, "Let us not take his life."
lines.zh: 約瑟的哥哥流便想救約瑟，所以他說：「我們不可要他的命。」

lines.en: "Throw him into this empty well here in the desert."
lines.zh: 「把他丟在這曠野裡的這口空井吧。」

lines.en: So when Joseph came to his brothers, they attacked him.
lines.zh: 所以當約瑟來到他哥哥們那裡時，他們就攻擊了他。

lines.en: They took the coat their father had given Joseph and threw him into the well.
lines.zh: 他們奪走了父親給約瑟的那件彩衣，並把他丟進井裡。

lines.en: Then they saw a group of men from Midian coming toward them.
lines.zh: 接著他們看到一群米甸人朝他們走來。

lines.en: Judah thought it would be a good idea to sell Joseph to these men.
lines.zh: 猶大認為把約瑟賣給這些人是個好主意。

lines.en: So the brothers sold Joseph to the traders for 20 shekels.
lines.zh: 於是哥哥們以二十舍客勒的價錢把約瑟賣給了那些商人。

lines.en: The brothers then took the coat of many colors back to their father and made him think that Joseph had been killed.
lines.zh: 然後哥哥們帶著那件彩衣回到父親那裡，讓他以為約瑟已經被殺了。

lines.en: Israel wept for his beloved son.
lines.zh: 以色列為他心愛的兒子哀哭。

lines.en: Meanwhile, Joseph was taken as a slave to Egypt to work in the house of a man named Potiphar, one of Pharaoh's officials and the captain of the guard.
lines.zh: 同時，約瑟被當作奴隸帶到埃及，在一個名叫波提乏的人家裡工作，這人是法老的臣宰，也是護衛長。

lines.en: Joseph's story was only just beginning.
lines.zh: 約瑟的故事才剛開始。

lines.en: When the Israelites were in the desert, God gave them a special set of rules called the Ten Commandments.
lines.zh: 當以色列人在曠野時，神賜給他們一套特別的律例，稱為十誡。

lines.en: The people were afraid to hear from God.
lines.zh: 百姓害怕聽見神的聲音。

lines.en: So, God spoke these commandments to Moses and Moses told the people.
lines.zh: 所以，神將這些誡命告訴摩西，摩西再告訴百姓。

lines.en: "Do not put any other gods in place of me."
lines.zh: 「除了我以外，你不可有別的神。」

lines.en: "Do not worship false gods."
lines.zh: 「不可敬拜假神。」

lines.en: "Do not misuse the name of God."
lines.zh: 「不可妄稱神的名。」

lines.en: "Remember the Sabbath day."
lines.zh: 「當記念安息日。」

lines.en: "Honor your father and mother."
lines.zh: 「當孝敬父母。」

lines.en: "Do not murder."
lines.zh: 「不可殺人。」

lines.en: "Do not commit adultery."
lines.zh: 「不可姦淫。」

lines.en: "Do not steal."
lines.zh: 「不可偷盜。」

lines.en: "Do not tell lies about your neighbor."
lines.zh: 「不可說謊陷害你的鄰舍。」

lines.en: "Do not want to have anything your neighbor owns."
lines.zh: 「不可貪圖你鄰舍所擁有的一切。」

lines.en: Then, God wrote the commandments on two stone tablets and gave them to Moses.
lines.zh: 然後，神將這些誡命寫在兩塊石版上，交給了摩西。

lines.en: God told Moses that he must teach the people to obey the rules and do all that God had commanded.
lines.zh: 神吩咐摩西，他必須教導百姓遵守這些律例，並遵行神所吩咐的一切。

lines.en: When the Israelites followed God's commandments, they would show the world they lived differently than all others and that they were God's chosen people.
lines.zh: 當以色列人遵行神的誡命時，他們便向世界展現出他們的生活方式與眾不同，並且他們是神所揀選的子民。

lines.en: This is Moses.
lines.zh: 這是摩西。

lines.en: Moses was the leader God chose to lead his chosen people, the Israelites, out of Egypt.
lines.zh: 摩西是神揀選的領袖，要帶領祂的選民以色列人出埃及。

lines.en: After God showed his miraculous power in Egypt, he led the Israelites through the Red Sea and towards the promised land.
lines.zh: 神在埃及彰顯祂奇妙的大能之後，就帶領以色列人過紅海，往應許之地去。

lines.en: They followed God, who showed himself as a cloud by day and a fire by night.
lines.zh: 他們跟隨神，神白天在雲柱中、夜間在火柱中向他們顯現。

lines.en: A few months after the Israelites left Egypt, they came to the desert of Sinai and camped there in front of the mountain.
lines.zh: 以色列人出埃及幾個月後，來到西奈的曠野，就在山前安營。

lines.en: God gave the Israelites a special set of rules called the Ten Commandments.
lines.zh: 神賜給以色列人一套特別的規條，稱為十誡。

lines.en: Moses climbed up to the mountain to hear from God, but the people were afraid.
lines.zh: 摩西爬上山去聽神的話，但百姓都很害怕。

lines.en: While the people remained a long way off, the Lord spoke to Moses and gave him many more commandments and instructions for the people of Israel to follow.
lines.zh: 百姓遠遠地站著，耶和華對摩西說話，又給他許多誡命和指示，要以色列人遵行。

lines.en: Then God wrote the commandments on two stone tablets and gave them to Moses.
lines.zh: 神把誡命寫在兩塊石版上，交給摩西。

lines.en: God told Moses that he must teach the people to obey the rules and do all that God had commanded.
lines.zh: 神告訴摩西，他必須教導百姓遵守這些規條，照神所吩咐的一切去行。

lines.en: When the Israelites followed God's commandments, they would show the world they lived differently than all the others and that they were God's chosen people.
lines.zh: 以色列人遵行神的誡命時，就會讓世人看見，他們的生活與眾不同，他們是神的選民。

lines.en: The people saw that Moses took a long time to come down from the mountain and they didn't know what happened to him.
lines.zh: 百姓見摩西遲遲不下山，不知道他遭遇了甚麼事。

lines.en: So they gathered around Aaron and asked him to make a god that could lead them.
lines.zh: 於是他們聚集到亞倫那裡，要他造一個能帶領他們的神。

lines.en: Aaron told them to give him their gold and he made it into a metal statue of a god that looked like a calf.
lines.zh: 亞倫叫他們把金子交給他，他把金子鑄成一尊像牛犢的神像。

lines.en: Then the people said, "Israel, here is your god who brought you up out of Egypt."
lines.zh: 百姓就說：「以色列啊，這是領你出埃及的神！」

lines.en: Aaron built an altar in front of the calf and declared the next day a feast day.
lines.zh: 亞倫在牛犢面前築壇，宣告明天要向耶和華守節。

lines.en: They sacrificed to the calf, celebrated, and danced wildly in front of their god.
lines.zh: 他們向牛犢獻祭、慶祝，在他們的神面前狂歡跳舞。

lines.en: The Lord spoke to Moses and told him to go down the mountain because of what the people were doing.
lines.zh: 耶和華對摩西說話，因百姓所做的事，吩咐他下山去。

lines.en: God told Moses that he would destroy the Israelites, but make a new nation out of Moses' family.
lines.zh: 神告訴摩西，祂要滅絕以色列人，卻要使摩西的家族成為大國。

lines.en: But Moses asked the Lord to have mercy on his people.
lines.zh: 但摩西求耶和華憐憫祂的百姓。

lines.en: Then the Lord took pity on his people.
lines.zh: 於是耶和華憐恤祂的百姓。

lines.en: He didn't destroy them as he said he would.
lines.zh: 祂沒有照所說的毀滅他們。

lines.en: Moses turned and went down the mountain.
lines.zh: 摩西轉身下山。

lines.en: He had two tablets that God had written in his hands.
lines.zh: 他手裡拿著神親手寫的兩塊法版。

lines.en: Joshua, Moses' assistant, heard the noise of the people shouting.
lines.zh: 摩西的助手約書亞聽見百姓呼喊的聲音。

lines.en: So he said to Moses, "It sounds like war in the camp."
lines.zh: 他就對摩西說：「營裡有爭戰的聲音。」

lines.en: But Moses said it was the sound of singing.
lines.zh: 摩西卻說，那是唱歌的聲音。

lines.en: As Moses approached the camp, he saw the calf and what the people were doing.
lines.zh: 摩西走近營地，看見牛犢，也看見百姓所做的事。

lines.en: So he was very angry.
lines.zh: 他就非常憤怒。

lines.en: He threw the tablets out of his hands and they broke into pieces at the foot of the mountain.
lines.zh: 他把兩塊法版從手裡扔下，在山腳下摔碎了。

lines.en: He took the calf the people had made.
lines.zh: 他把百姓所造的牛犢拿來，

lines.en: He burned it in the fire.
lines.zh: 用火焚燒，

lines.en: Then he ground it into powder.
lines.zh: 又磨得粉碎，

lines.en: He scattered it on the water and he made the Israelites drink it.
lines.zh: 撒在水面上，叫以色列人喝。

lines.en: Moses asked Aaron why he would let the people do this.
lines.zh: 摩西問亞倫，為甚麼讓百姓這樣做。

lines.en: Aaron said it was the people's fault and that when he threw the gold into the fire, it came out as a calf.
lines.zh: 亞倫說這是百姓的錯，又說他把金子扔進火裡，這牛犢就出來了。

lines.en: Moses said, "Anyone on the Lord's side, come to me."
lines.zh: 摩西說：「凡屬耶和華的，都要到我這裡來！」

lines.en: All the Levites joined him.
lines.zh: 利未人都聚集到他那裡。

lines.en: Moses had the Levites punish the people for their sin.
lines.zh: 摩西叫利未人為百姓的罪懲罰他們。

lines.en: And the next day, Moses turned the people over to the Lord, but asked that he forgive their sin.
lines.zh: 第二天，摩西把百姓交在耶和華面前，求祂赦免他們的罪。

lines.en: The Lord sent a plague because of what the people did with the calf, but he didn't destroy the nation of Israel, even though they had turned away from him.
lines.zh: 耶和華因百姓造牛犢的事降下災殃，但祂沒有毀滅以色列，雖然他們背離了祂。

lines.en: Later, God had Moses make two new stone tablets, and God wrote on them the same words that were on the first tablets.
lines.zh: 後來，神叫摩西另鑿兩塊石版，神在上面寫了與先前那兩塊相同的字。

lines.en: God continued to speak with Moses and guide him as he led the Israelites.
lines.zh: 神繼續與摩西說話，在他帶領以色列人的路上引導他。

lines.en: This is Deborah.
lines.zh: 這是底波拉。

lines.en: Deborah was a judge of Israel and a prophet of God.
lines.zh: 底波拉是以色列的士師，也是神的先知。

lines.en: It was her job to lead the Israelites in the way God wanted, and to tell the people what God wanted her to say.
lines.zh: 她的職責是照神的心意帶領以色列人，並把神要她說的話告訴百姓。

lines.en: She would sit under a palm tree, and the Israelites would come up to her so she could help them make a decision when they didn't know what to do.
lines.zh: 她常坐在一棵棕樹下，以色列人不知道該怎麼辦時，就上她那裡去，請她幫忙做決定。

lines.en: There was a commander named Sisera, who was in charge of the army of Canaan, who were enemies of Israel.
lines.zh: 有一位將軍名叫西西拉，他統領迦南的軍隊，迦南人是以色列的仇敵。

lines.en: Sisera and his army treated the Israelites very badly for twenty years.
lines.zh: 西西拉和他的軍隊欺壓以色列人二十年。

lines.en: So the Israelites cried out to the Lord for help.
lines.zh: 以色列人就呼求耶和華幫助。

lines.en: Deborah sent for a man named Barak and said, "The Lord, the God of Israel, is giving you a command."
lines.zh: 底波拉派人叫一個名叫巴拉的人來，對他說：「耶和華以色列的神吩咐你。」

lines.en: "He says, 'Go, take ten thousand men from the tribes of Naphtali and Zebulun with you.'"
lines.zh: 「祂說：『你要從拿弗他利和西布倫支派中率領一萬人。』」

lines.en: "'Then lead them up to Mount Tabor.'"
lines.zh: 「『帶他們上他泊山。』」

lines.en: "'I will lead Sisera into a trap. There I will hand him over to you.'"
lines.zh: 「『我必使西西拉落入圈套，把他交在你手中。』」

lines.en: Barak said to her, "If you go with me, I'll go. But if you don't go with me, I won't go."
lines.zh: 巴拉對她說：「你若同我去，我就去；你若不同我去，我就不去。」

lines.en: "All right, I'll go with you."
lines.zh: 「好吧，我必與你同去。」

lines.en: "But because of the way you are doing this, you won't receive any honor."
lines.zh: 「只是你這樣做，就得不著榮耀。」

lines.en: "Instead, the Lord will hand Sisera over to a woman."
lines.zh: 「因為耶和華要把西西拉交在一個婦人手裡。」

lines.en: So Barak gathered the army God commanded, and Deborah also went with him.
lines.zh: 巴拉就照神的吩咐召集軍隊，底波拉也與他同去。

lines.en: Sisera gathered together his nine hundred chariots and all his men.
lines.zh: 西西拉召集了他的九百輛鐵車和全軍。

lines.en: Then Deborah said to Barak, "Go! Today the Lord will hand Sisera over to you. Hasn't the Lord gone ahead of you?"
lines.zh: 底波拉對巴拉說：「起來！今日就是耶和華把西西拉交在你手的日子。耶和華豈不在你前頭行嗎？」

lines.en: So Barak and his men marched out, and the Lord drove Sisera away from the battlefield.
lines.zh: 巴拉就帶著軍隊出征，耶和華使西西拉從戰場上潰逃。

lines.en: All of Sisera's army was defeated, but Sisera ran away on foot to the tent of a woman named Jael.
lines.zh: 西西拉的全軍都被打敗了，西西拉卻徒步逃到一個名叫雅億的婦人的帳棚。

lines.en: Jael brought Sisera into her tent.
lines.zh: 雅億把西西拉迎進帳棚。

lines.en: He thought she was helping him, but she quietly defeated him as he slept.
lines.zh: 他以為她在幫他，她卻趁他熟睡時悄悄打敗了他。

lines.en: Barak came and saw that what God told Deborah had happened, and Sisera had been defeated by a woman.
lines.zh: 巴拉趕到，看見神對底波拉說的話應驗了：西西拉被一個婦人打敗。

lines.en: On that day, God brought Canaan under Israel's control.
lines.zh: 那一日，神使迦南人被以色列人制伏。

lines.en: Deborah and Barak sang a song praising God for what he had done.
lines.zh: 底波拉和巴拉唱歌讚美神所做的事。

lines.en: And Israel was at peace again for forty years.
lines.zh: 以色列又太平了四十年。

lines.en: This is David.
lines.zh: 這是大衛。

lines.en: David was a shepherd who lived in Israel.
lines.zh: 大衛是個牧羊人，住在以色列。

lines.en: Israel became a great nation that was ruled by judges, men and women who helped the people follow God.
lines.zh: 以色列成為一個偉大的國家，由士師統治，這些男女幫助百姓跟隨神。

lines.en: But the people asked for a king so they could be like the other nations.
lines.zh: 但百姓要求立一個王，這樣他們就能像其他國家一樣。

lines.en: God warned them through the prophet Samuel that a king would not be the best choice for them, but the people wanted a king anyway.
lines.zh: 神透過先知撒母耳警告他們，立王對他們來說不是最好的選擇，但百姓仍然想要一個王。

lines.en: So God chose a man named Saul and had Samuel anoint him.
lines.zh: 於是神揀選了一個名叫掃羅的人，並讓撒母耳膏抹他。

lines.en: Saul became the king of Israel.
lines.zh: 掃羅成為了以色列的王。

lines.en: Saul started out as a good king, but he started making wrong choices and did not follow God as he should.
lines.zh: 掃羅一開始是個好王，但他開始做出錯誤的選擇，並且沒有照他所應該的那樣跟隨神。

lines.en: God was sad that he made Saul king, so God sent Samuel to the house of Jesse in Bethlehem because God had chosen one of Jesse's sons to be the new king of Israel.
lines.zh: 神因為立掃羅為王而感到憂傷，所以神差遣撒母耳去伯利恆耶西的家，因為神已經揀選了耶西的一個兒子成為以色列的新王。

lines.en: Jesse's oldest son was strong and handsome.
lines.zh: 耶西的大兒子又強壯又英俊。

lines.en: Samuel thought that surely God would choose this son to be king.
lines.zh: 撒母耳以為神肯定會揀選這個兒子作王。

lines.en: But God said, "The Lord does not look at the things people look at. People look at the outside of a person, but the Lord looks at what is in the heart."
lines.zh: 但神說：「耶和華不像人看人。人是看外貌，耶和華是看內心。」

lines.en: One by one, Jesse had seven more of his sons walk in front of Samuel.
lines.zh: 耶西讓他的另外七個兒子一個接一個地從撒母耳面前走過。

lines.en: But Samuel said, "The Lord hasn't chosen any of them."
lines.zh: 但撒母耳說：「耶和華沒有揀選他們其中任何一個。」

lines.en: Samuel asked if Jesse had any other sons, and Jesse said, "My youngest son is taking care of the sheep."
lines.zh: 撒母耳問耶西是否還有其他兒子，耶西說：「我最小的兒子正在放羊。」

lines.en: Samuel asked Jesse to bring the son to him, and Jesse had David brought in from the fields.
lines.zh: 撒母耳請耶西把這兒子帶過來，耶西就讓人把大衛從田野裡帶了進來。

lines.en: God said to Samuel, "This is the one."
lines.zh: 神對撒母耳說：「這就是那人。」

lines.en: So Samuel anointed David by pouring oil on his head to show that God had chosen David to be the next king of Israel.
lines.zh: 於是撒母耳藉著把油倒在大衛頭上來膏抹他，表明神已經揀選大衛作以色列的下一任王。

lines.en: From that day on, the Spirit of the Lord came powerfully on David.
lines.zh: 從那日起，耶和華的靈就大大感動大衛。

lines.en: David went on to serve King Saul, defeat a giant with a stone and a sling, and many years later he did become king.
lines.zh: 大衛接著去服事掃羅王，用一塊石頭和一個機弦打敗了一個巨人，多年後他確實成為了王。

lines.en: David served God's purpose in his own generation.
lines.zh: 大衛在他自己的世代服事了神的旨意。

lines.en: He wasn't a perfect king, but he was a good king because he was a man after God's own heart.
lines.zh: 他不是一個完美的王，但他是一個好王，因為他是一個合神心意的人。

lines.en: This is Nehemiah, who was a Jewish man who worked for a Persian king, Artaxerxes, the king of Babylon.
lines.zh: 這是尼希米，他是猶太人，在波斯王亞達薛西手下做事，那王也統治巴比倫。

lines.en: Many of the Jews had been sent to Babylon years before because they had disobeyed God.
lines.zh: 多年前，許多猶太人因為違背神，被擄到巴比倫。

lines.en: One day Nehemiah heard a report that the Jews who had returned to Judah were having a hard time, and that the walls of Jerusalem were broken down and the gates had been burned.
lines.zh: 有一天，尼希米聽到消息：回到猶大的猶太人處境艱難，耶路撒冷的城牆被拆毀，城門也被火焚燒。

lines.en: This made Nehemiah sad.
lines.zh: 這讓尼希米非常憂傷。

lines.en: He didn't eat any food for days and prayed to God for the Jews.
lines.zh: 他好幾天不吃東西，為猶太人向神禱告。

lines.en: He told God he was sorry for the wrong things he and his people had done.
lines.zh: 他向神認罪，為自己和同胞所犯的錯懺悔。

lines.en: He reminded God of his promises, and that God had said, "If you obey my commands, I will gather you together again."
lines.zh: 他求神記念祂的應許，神曾說：「你們若遵守我的誡命，我必再招聚你們。」

lines.en: Nehemiah asked for God to give him success as he went to ask the king for help.
lines.zh: 尼希米求神在他去求王幫助時，使他順利。

lines.en: Nehemiah went to do his job for the king.
lines.zh: 尼希米照常去服事王。

lines.en: The king asked why Nehemiah was sad.
lines.zh: 王問尼希米為甚麼面帶愁容。

lines.en: So Nehemiah told the king about his people in Judah.
lines.zh: 尼希米就把猶大同胞的事告訴王。

lines.en: Nehemiah prayed and told the king he wanted to rebuild the city of Jerusalem.
lines.zh: 尼希米默默禱告，然後告訴王，他想重建耶路撒冷城。

lines.en: He asked for letters from the king that would help him travel safely to Jerusalem and get the supplies he needed to rebuild the city.
lines.zh: 他求王賜下詔書，讓他平安抵達耶路撒冷，並取得重建城所需的材料。

lines.en: God helped Nehemiah, and the king gave Nehemiah all he asked for.
lines.zh: 神幫助尼希米，王就把他所求的都賜給他。

lines.en: Nehemiah went to Jerusalem and checked out the walls.
lines.zh: 尼希米到了耶路撒冷，察看城牆。

lines.en: He went to the people and said, "Come on, let's rebuild the wall of Jerusalem."
lines.zh: 他到百姓那裡說：「來吧，我們來重建耶路撒冷的城牆！」

lines.en: And the people agreed and started that good work.
lines.zh: 百姓都同意，就開始做這美好的工作。

lines.en: Meanwhile, there were some officials from nearby lands who heard Nehemiah was rebuilding the wall and were upset.
lines.zh: 這時，鄰近地方的一些官員聽說尼希米在重建城牆，就很不高興。

lines.en: They laughed at the Jews and made fun of them.
lines.zh: 他們嗤笑猶太人，嘲弄他們。

lines.en: But Nehemiah said, "The God of heaven will give us success. We serve him."
lines.zh: 尼希米卻說：「天上的神必使我們亨通，我們是事奉祂的。」

lines.en: Many Jews worked together to rebuild the wall, including the priests, men who worked with gold, a man who made perfume, leaders from nearby villages, servants, guards, traders, and daughters as well.
lines.zh: 許多猶太人同心重建城牆，包括祭司、金匠、做香料的、鄰近村莊的首領、僕人、守衛、商人，還有女兒們。

lines.en: All the people worked with all their hearts.
lines.zh: 百姓都全心全意地做工。

lines.en: The officials from other lands planned to fight the Jews, but the Jews prayed to God and put guards on duty day and night.
lines.zh: 外地的官員計劃攻擊猶太人，但猶太人向神禱告，並安排守衛晝夜看守。

lines.en: Nehemiah stationed people to defend the city where it was weak.
lines.zh: 尼希米在城牆薄弱的地方派人防守。

lines.en: From that day on, half of the people did the work with swords at their sides, and the other half were armed to defend the people working and the city.
lines.zh: 從那天起，一半的人腰間佩刀做工，另一半的人拿著兵器，保護做工的人和整座城。

lines.en: Nehemiah reminded them, "Our God will fight for us."
lines.zh: 尼希米提醒他們：「我們的神必為我們爭戰！」

lines.en: They worked from sunrise until the stars came out.
lines.zh: 他們從日出一直做到星宿出現。

lines.en: After fifty-two days, the city wall was finally finished.
lines.zh: 五十二天後，城牆終於完工了。

lines.en: All of Judah's enemies were afraid, because they realized that God helped the people finish the work.
lines.zh: 猶大所有的仇敵都懼怕了，因為他們知道這工作是神幫助百姓完成的。

lines.en: Jerusalem was large. It had a lot of room, but only a few people lived there.
lines.zh: 耶路撒冷城很大，有許多空間，住的人卻很少。

lines.en: So God gave Nehemiah the idea to gather more people to come and live in Jerusalem, now that the wall had been rebuilt.
lines.zh: 於是神感動尼希米：既然城牆已經重建，就招聚更多人來住在耶路撒冷。

lines.en: And many people returned home to Israel as God gathered his people together again.
lines.zh: 許多人回到故土，神再次招聚了祂的子民。

lines.en: A teacher of God's law named Ezra came and read the Book of the Law to all the people who could understand.
lines.zh: 一位名叫以斯拉的律法教師，向所有能聽明白的百姓宣讀律法書。

lines.en: Then they worshiped God and promised to follow God's commands.
lines.zh: 於是他們敬拜神，並承諾要遵行神的誡命。

lines.en: This is Daniel, who was a Jewish man who was taken to Babylon when he was very young.
lines.zh: 這是但以理，他是個猶太人，年紀很小就被擄到巴比倫。

lines.en: Daniel loved God and followed God's rules.
lines.zh: 但以理愛神，遵守神的律例。

lines.en: He talked to God three times a day and asked God for help often.
lines.zh: 他一天三次向神禱告，常常求神幫助。

lines.en: Daniel served in the Babylonian king's court for many years, and under many kings.
lines.zh: 但以理在巴比倫王的朝廷中事奉多年，歷經好幾位君王。

lines.en: Daniel always proved himself to be more capable than all the other court officials.
lines.zh: 但以理總是證明自己比朝中所有官員都更有才幹。

lines.en: Daniel was serving under King Darius, and because of his great abilities, the king made plans to place him in charge of the entire empire.
lines.zh: 但以理在大利烏王手下任職，因他才能出眾，王打算立他治理全國。

lines.en: The other court officials searched for some fault in Daniel, but they couldn't find anything wrong with him.
lines.zh: 其他官員想找但以理的把柄，卻找不到他有任何錯處。

lines.en: He was faithful, responsible, and completely trustworthy.
lines.zh: 他忠心、盡責，完全值得信賴。

lines.en: The court officials realized the only way to get at Daniel would be to challenge his faith.
lines.zh: 官員們意識到，要對付但以理，唯一的辦法就是從他的信仰下手。

lines.en: So they went to King Darius and advised him to make a law that for the next thirty days, any person who prays to anyone except King Darius will be thrown into the lions' den.
lines.zh: 於是他們去見大利烏王，建議他立一條法令：三十天內，凡向大利烏王以外的任何對象祈求的，必被扔進獅子坑。

lines.en: King Darius signed this law, and once a Babylonian king signed a law, it could not be overruled.
lines.zh: 大利烏王簽署了這條法令；巴比倫王一旦簽了法令，就不能更改。

lines.en: When Daniel learned of this law, he went home and knelt down as he always did to pray in his room, with the windows open towards Jerusalem.
lines.zh: 但以理知道了這條法令，就回到家裡，照常在房間裡跪下禱告，窗戶開向耶路撒冷。

lines.en: He prayed three times a day, just as he always had done, giving thanks to God and asking for his help.
lines.zh: 他一日三次禱告，跟往常一樣，感謝神，也求神幫助。

lines.en: The officials went to Daniel's house and found him praying.
lines.zh: 官員們到但以理家，發現他正在禱告。

lines.en: They went to the king and reminded him of the law.
lines.zh: 他們去見王，提醒他那條法令。

lines.en: Then they said that Daniel had been found praying to God three times a day.
lines.zh: 接著他們說，但以理被人看見一天三次向神禱告。

lines.en: When the king heard this, he was very upset.
lines.zh: 王聽了這話，非常難過。

lines.en: And he spent the whole day trying to think of a way to save Daniel.
lines.zh: 他花了一整天想辦法要救但以理。

lines.en: By that evening, the court officials came back to the king and reminded him that no law signed by the Babylonian king could be overruled.
lines.zh: 到了傍晚，官員們又來見王，提醒他巴比倫王所簽的法令都不能更改。

lines.en: So at last the king gave orders for Daniel to be thrown into the lions' den.
lines.zh: 王終於下令，把但以理扔進獅子坑。

lines.en: The king said to him, "May your God, whom you serve faithfully, rescue you."
lines.zh: 王對他說：「你所常事奉的神，必救你！」

lines.en: Then the lions' den was sealed shut with Daniel inside.
lines.zh: 然後獅子坑被封住，但以理在裡面。

lines.en: The king spent the night fasting and couldn't sleep.
lines.zh: 王整夜禁食，無法入睡。

lines.en: Then very early in the morning, the king hurried to the lions' den.
lines.zh: 次日清早，王急忙往獅子坑去。

lines.en: He called out, "Daniel, was your God able to rescue you from the lions?"
lines.zh: 他喊道：「但以理啊，你的神能救你脫離獅子嗎？」

lines.en: And Daniel answered, "Long live the king!"
lines.zh: 但以理回答：「願王萬歲！」

lines.en: "My God sent his angel to shut the lions' mouths so that they would not hurt me, for I have been found innocent in his sight."
lines.zh: 「我的神差遣使者封住獅子的口，叫獅子不傷我，因我在神面前無辜。」

lines.en: The king was overjoyed and ordered that Daniel be taken out of the lions' den.
lines.zh: 王非常歡喜，吩咐人把但以理從坑裡拉上來。

lines.en: Then the king ordered the men who had schemed against Daniel to be thrown into the lions' den as punishment.
lines.zh: 王又下令，把那些設計陷害但以理的人扔進獅子坑作為懲罰。

lines.en: Daniel was safe. There was not a scratch on him, for he trusted in God.
lines.zh: 但以理平安無事，身上毫無傷損，因為他信靠神。

lines.en: This is Jesus.
lines.zh: 這位是耶穌。

lines.en: He is the Son of God and the Savior of the world.
lines.zh: 祂是神的兒子，也是世人的救主。

lines.en: While Jesus was on Earth, he taught everyone about God's love and performed many miracles like healing people.
lines.zh: 耶穌在世上的時候，教導大家關於神的愛，並行了許多神蹟，例如醫治人。

lines.en: One day a crowd gathered around Jesus, so he went up to a mountain side and sat down.
lines.zh: 有一天，群眾聚集在耶穌周圍，所以祂上了一座山，坐了下來。

lines.en: His disciples gathered around him and he began to teach them about what was right and wrong, the kingdom of heaven, and how to treat other people.
lines.zh: 祂的門徒聚集在祂身邊，祂就開始教導他們什麼是對與錯、天國的道理，以及如何對待別人。

lines.en: He taught them about prayer and said, "When you pray, do not be like those who only pretend to be holy."
lines.zh: 祂教導他們關於禱告的事，並說：「你們禱告的時候，不要像那些只會假裝神聖的人。」

lines.en: "They love to stand and pray in the synagogues and on the street corners."
lines.zh: 「他們喜歡站在會堂裡和十字路口上禱告。」

lines.en: "They want to be seen by other people."
lines.zh: 「他們想要被人看見。」

lines.en: "What I'm about to tell you is true."
lines.zh: 「我接下來要告訴你們的是實話。」

lines.en: "They have received their complete reward."
lines.zh: 「他們已經得到了他們全部的賞賜。」

lines.en: "When you pray, go into your room, close the door and pray to your Father who can't be seen."
lines.zh: 「你禱告的時候，要進你的內屋，關上門，向看不見的天父禱告。」

lines.en: "Your Father will reward you because he sees what you do secretly."
lines.zh: 「你的天父會賞賜你，因為祂看見你在暗中所做的事。」

lines.en: "When you pray, do not keep talking on and on."
lines.zh: 「你們禱告的時候，不要喋喋不休。」

lines.en: "That is what ungodly people do."
lines.zh: 「那是不敬虔的人所做的。」

lines.en: "They think they will be heard because they talk a lot."
lines.zh: 「他們以為話說得多就會蒙垂聽。」

lines.en: "Do not be like them."
lines.zh: 「你們不可像他們。」

lines.en: "Your Father knows what you need even before you ask him."
lines.zh: 「因為在你們祈求以先，你們的天父就已經知道你們的需要了。」

lines.en: He explained, "This is how you should pray."
lines.zh: 祂解釋說：「所以，你們要這樣禱告。」

lines.en: "Our Father in heaven, may your name be honored."
lines.zh: 「我們在天上的父，願人都尊祢的名為聖。」

lines.en: "May your kingdom come."
lines.zh: 「願祢的國降臨。」

lines.en: "May what you want to happen be done on Earth as it is done in heaven."
lines.zh: 「願祢的旨意行在地上，如同行在天上。」

lines.en: "Give us today our daily bread and forgive us our sins, just as we also have forgiven those who sin against us."
lines.zh: 「今日賜給我們日用的飲食，赦免我們的罪，如同我們也饒恕了得罪我們的人。」

lines.en: "Keep us from sinning when we are tempted."
lines.zh: 「當我們受試探時，保守我們免於犯罪。」

lines.en: "Save us from the evil one."
lines.zh: 「救我們脫離那惡者。」

lines.en: These are the apostles. They followed Jesus during his time on earth.
lines.zh: 這些是使徒，耶穌在世的時候，他們一直跟隨祂。

lines.en: Before Jesus went to heaven, he told them to stay in Jerusalem until God sent the gift he promised.
lines.zh: 耶穌升天以前，吩咐他們留在耶路撒冷，等候神所應許的恩賜。

lines.en: So after Jesus went to heaven, the apostles stayed in Jerusalem along with the other people who believed in Jesus.
lines.zh: 所以耶穌升天以後，使徒們和其他信耶穌的人一起留在耶路撒冷。

lines.en: One day they were all gathered together when there was a sound from heaven like a mighty windstorm.
lines.zh: 有一天，他們都聚集在一起，忽然從天上有響聲，好像一陣大風。

lines.en: Then what looked like flames appeared and settled on each of them, and everyone was filled with the Holy Spirit.
lines.zh: 接著有像火焰的舌頭顯現，分開落在他們各人頭上，他們就都被聖靈充滿。

lines.en: The Holy Spirit gave them the ability to speak in other languages, and so they started speaking.
lines.zh: 聖靈賜給他們說別國語言的能力，他們就開始說起來。

lines.en: At that time, there were devout Jews from every nation living in Jerusalem.
lines.zh: 那時，有從各國來的虔誠猶太人住在耶路撒冷。

lines.en: When they heard the loud noise, they came running to see what it was.
lines.zh: 他們聽見這巨大的聲響，就跑來看是怎麼回事。

lines.en: When they saw the believers speaking in their own languages, they were shocked and amazed.
lines.zh: 他們聽見信徒說著自己家鄉的語言，都驚訝萬分。

lines.en: They wondered, "How can this be? These people are from Galilee, and yet we hear them speaking in our own native languages about the wonderful things God has done!"
lines.zh: 他們心想：「這是怎麼回事？這些人都是加利利人，我們怎麼聽見他們用我們的鄉談，講說神的大作為呢？」

lines.en: "What can this mean?"
lines.zh: 「這是甚麼意思呢？」

lines.en: But others in the crowd didn't believe that it was really a miracle, and thought the believers were just acting oddly.
lines.zh: 但人群中也有人不相信這是神蹟，以為信徒們只是舉止怪異。

lines.en: Then Peter stepped forward and shouted to the crowd, "Listen carefully, all of you!"
lines.zh: 彼得就站出來，向眾人高聲說：「你們都要留心聽！」

lines.en: He told them that they were not acting strangely, but that this was from God.
lines.zh: 他告訴他們，這些人不是行為怪異，這是從神來的。

lines.en: He reminded them that God said this would happen long ago.
lines.zh: 他提醒他們，神很久以前就說過這事要發生。

lines.en: Then Peter told them about how Jesus was crucified, but then raised to life again, just as God had said he would be.
lines.zh: 接著彼得告訴他們，耶穌怎樣被釘十字架，又照神所說的復活了。

lines.en: He told them that Jesus was now in heaven, and that God had given the Holy Spirit to them as he had promised.
lines.zh: 他告訴他們，耶穌現在在天上，神也照祂所應許的，把聖靈賜給了他們。

lines.en: Peter's words changed what the people thought and felt, and they asked, "Brothers, what should we do?"
lines.zh: 彼得的話改變了眾人的想法和感受，他們就問：「弟兄們，我們當怎樣行？」

lines.en: Peter told them, "Each of you must repent of your sins and turn to God, and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins."
lines.zh: 彼得說：「你們各人要悔改，歸向神，奉耶穌基督的名受洗，叫你們的罪得赦。」

lines.en: "Then you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit."
lines.zh: 「就必領受所賜的聖靈。」

lines.en: Peter continued to preach to the crowd for a long time, and those who believed what Peter said were baptized.
lines.zh: 彼得繼續向群眾講了很久，凡相信他話的人都受了洗。

lines.en: Three thousand people were baptized and added to the church that day.
lines.zh: 那天受洗加入教會的約有三千人。

lines.en: Then all the believers listened to the apostles' teaching and practiced what they taught.
lines.zh: 所有信徒都聽從使徒的教導，並且實踐出來。

lines.en: They met together in fellowship, shared meals, and prayed together.
lines.zh: 他們彼此交接、一起用餐、一同禱告。

lines.en: They were amazed as the apostles performed many miraculous signs and wonders.
lines.zh: 使徒們行了許多神蹟奇事，眾人都很驚奇。

lines.en: All the believers met together in one place and shared everything they had.
lines.zh: 信的人都聚在一處，凡物公用。

lines.en: They helped those in need, worshiped together at the temple every day, met in homes for the Lord's Supper, and shared their meals with great joy.
lines.zh: 他們幫助有需要的人，天天同心在聖殿敬拜，在家中擘餅記念主，歡歡喜喜地一同吃飯。

lines.en: All while praising God and enjoying each other.
lines.zh: 他們讚美神，也彼此享受相處的時光。

lines.en: And each day God added to their fellowship those who were being saved.
lines.zh: 主將得救的人天天加給他們。

lessons.title: Does God Play Favorites?
lessons.summaryZh: 神不偏待人，在祂的國度裡沒有比較的空間，我們只需專注於祂賦予的使命。

lines.en: Who do you compare yourself to?
lines.zh: 你會把自己和誰比較？

lines.en: Even though they don't mean to, who makes you feel like you're not quite as good as they are?
lines.zh: 即使他們不是有意的，有誰會讓你覺得自己比不上他們？

lines.en: Maybe because they seem better at the job, or better at mothering, smarter, skinnier—all the things, right?
lines.zh: 也許是因為他們在工作上表現更好，或是更會當媽媽、更聰明、更苗條——各方面都更好，對吧？

lines.en: I tend to compare myself to people that I'm closest to, like my sister and my friends and people at work.
lines.zh: 我傾向於和最親近的人比較，像是我的姊妹、朋友和同事。

lines.en: In my mind, when I naturally see them excelling at something, I look at myself and I size myself up to them.
lines.zh: 在我心裡，當我自然而然看到他們在某件事上表現優異時，我就會看看自己，並且拿自己跟他們比較。

lines.en: And that's why Scripture like today's verse starts to heal my wrong way of thinking about myself.
lines.zh: 這就是為什麼像今天這段經文開始醫治我對自己錯誤的想法。

lines.en: See, God does not size us up.
lines.zh: 你看，神並不會那樣評估我們。

lines.en: He does not show favoritism.
lines.zh: 祂不偏待人。

lines.en: In fact, if anything, He sees people like me who feel weak and less than, and He affirms that we are worthy of being part of His kingdom.
lines.zh: 事實上，如果有什麼不同的話，祂看見像我這樣感到軟弱和不如人的人，並且祂肯定我們配得成為祂國度的一份子。

lines.en: That's what Paul was talking about as he wrote to the Galatian church.
lines.zh: 這正是保羅在寫給加拉太教會的信中所談到的。

lines.en: He reminded them that he was the least of the apostles, but that God had commissioned him for this great work of spreading the gospel.
lines.zh: 他提醒他們，他是使徒中最小的，但神還是委派他去完成傳揚福音這項偉大的工作。

lines.en: He said, "For those who were held in high esteem—whatever they were makes no difference to me; God does not show favoritism—they added nothing to my message."
lines.zh: 他說：「至於那些有名望的，不論他是何等人，都與我無干。神不偏待人。那些有名望的，並沒有加增我甚麼。」

lines.en: The people others thought were awesome didn't affect Paul because he knew that God didn't favor them over him, or him over them.
lines.zh: 那些別人認為很了不起的人並沒有影響保羅，因為他知道神不會偏袒他們勝過他，也不會偏袒他勝過他們。

lines.en: God doesn't play our earthly favoritism games.
lines.zh: 神不玩我們世上那種偏心對待的遊戲。

lines.en: I need that same reminder so badly—that I don't need anyone to add, including myself, to any of the missions God is giving me.
lines.zh: 我非常需要同樣的提醒——我不需要任何人，包括我自己，來加添神所賜給我的任何使命。

lines.en: Others may naturally excel more than I do, but God is the one equipping me to do the job that He's called me to.
lines.zh: 別人天生可能比我更優秀，但神是裝備我去做祂呼召我去做之工的那位。

lines.en: And the same is true of you.
lines.zh: 而你也是如此。

lines.en: God isn't any more or less impressed with you than He is with me.
lines.zh: 神對你的看重，不會比對我多，也不會比對我少。

lines.en: He's called you to partner in His great kingdom, to share in the power of the gospel as you live out His love to those around you like only you can.
lines.zh: 祂呼召你參與在祂偉大的國度中，當你以只有你能做到的方式，向周遭的人活出祂的愛時，你就在分享福音的大能。

lines.en: Don't diminish that.
lines.zh: 不要貶低這一點。

lines.en: There's no room for comparison in God's kingdom.
lines.zh: 在神的國度裡，沒有比較的空間。

lines.en: So let's get a little confidence in what God is doing in us today.
lines.zh: 因此，讓我們對神今天在我們裡面所做的工作多一點信心吧。

lessons.title: Moved by Compassion
lessons.summaryZh: 貼近他人的困境能喚醒我們的憐憫之心，並讓生命充滿神所賜的使命感。

lines.en: I have a friend who works on the streets of Compton, near LA, sharing Jesus with teenagers.
lines.zh: 我有一位朋友在洛杉磯附近的康普頓街頭工作，向青少年分享耶穌。

lines.en: Their stories are crazy and so is the impact he’s having.
lines.zh: 他們的故事非常不可思議，而他所帶來的影響力也是如此。

lines.en: I was on the phone with him the other day and he brought up the story of the Good Samaritan.
lines.zh: 前幾天我和他通電話時，他提到了好撒馬利亞人的故事。

lines.en: You probably know it.
lines.zh: 你可能知道這個故事。

lines.en: Jewish guy gets beat up and left on the road.
lines.zh: 一個猶太人被打，並被丟在路邊。

lines.en: Priests pass by on the other side.
lines.zh: 祭司從另一邊走過去。

lines.en: Levite passed by on the other side.
lines.zh: 利未人也從另一邊走過去。

lines.en: They stayed far enough away to avoid feeling too bad about it all.
lines.zh: 他們保持著足夠的距離，以免對這一切感到太內疚。

lines.en: "But a Samaritan, as he traveled, came where the man was."
lines.zh: 「惟有一個撒馬利亞人行路來到那裡。」

lines.en: "And when he saw him, he took pity on him."
lines.zh: 「看見他就動了慈心。」

lines.en: This story has taken on more significance since my friend moved so close to the brokenness.
lines.zh: 自從我朋友如此貼近這些破碎的生命後，這個故事變得更具意義。

lines.en: He can’t help but do something about what he sees.
lines.zh: 看到這一切，他忍不住要採取一些行動。

lines.en: Being close awakens our compassion.
lines.zh: 貼近人群能喚醒我們的憐憫。

lines.en: Jesus said the Good Samaritan was being a good neighbor.
lines.zh: 耶穌說，這個好撒馬利亞人做了一個好鄰舍。

lines.en: I think the Jewish guy probably saw him as a hero.
lines.zh: 我想那個猶太人可能把他視為英雄。

lines.en: My friend is a neighbor/hero in the lives of these young people because he got close enough for his compassion to wake up.
lines.zh: 我的朋友成為了這些年輕人生命中的鄰舍與英雄，因為他足夠靠近，喚醒了他的憐憫。

lines.en: I can promise you that as his compassion moves him to action, his life is bursting with purpose.
lines.zh: 我可以向你保證，當他的憐憫驅使他採取行動時，他的生命便充滿了使命感。

lines.en: So if you find yourself wondering if your life matters these days, might I challenge you to get close enough to someone’s trouble to wake up your compassion and move you to action?
lines.zh: 因此，如果你最近在想自己的生命是否有意義，我可否挑戰你去貼近某人的困境，來喚醒你的憐憫並驅使你採取行動？

lines.en: It’s what Jesus did for us when He left heaven, getting close enough to see just how much we needed a hero, too.
lines.zh: 這正是耶穌為我們所做的，當祂離開天上，足夠靠近地看見我們也是多麼需要一位英雄。

lessons.title: The Low Places
lessons.summaryZh: 當我們身處低谷時，可以效法詩人向神傾吐哀傷、與朋友分享，並將盼望交託給神。

lines.en: One of my favorite musicians, singer songwriter named Gregory Alan Isakov.
lines.zh: 我最喜歡的音樂家之一，是一位名叫格雷戈里·艾倫·伊薩科夫的創作歌手。

lines.en: He has a song called "Dark, Dark, Dark."
lines.zh: 他有一首歌叫做《Dark, Dark, Dark》。

lines.en: And there's a line in it where he says, "The songs in my pocket just crumble apart.
lines.zh: 裡面有一句歌詞說：「我口袋裡的歌就這樣碎裂。

lines.en: Won't you sing me something for the dark, dark, dark."
lines.zh: 你能為這黑暗、黑暗、黑暗唱點什麼嗎？」

lines.en: I love that line because it's not a matter of if you will go through dark seasons, it's a matter of when.
lines.zh: 我很喜歡那句歌詞，因為我們是否會經歷黑暗的季節，不是會不會的問題，而是何時的問題。

lines.en: And when you do there are certain songs that just can't hold the weight of your pain.
lines.zh: 當你經歷時，有些歌就是無法承載你痛苦的重量。

lines.en: What you need in those seasons is a song for the dark.
lines.zh: 在那些季節裡，你需要的是一首為黑暗而唱的歌。

lines.en: Psalm 42 is a song for the dark.
lines.zh: 詩篇第42篇就是一首為黑暗而寫的歌。

lines.en: "My tears have been my food day and night," the Psalmist writes.
lines.zh: 詩人寫道：「我晝夜以眼淚當飲食。」

lines.en: Have you ever been there?
lines.zh: 你曾經歷過那種境地嗎？

lines.en: Maybe you're stumbling upon this video and you're there right now.
lines.zh: 也許你偶然點開這部影片，而你現在正處於那種境地。

lines.en: As a licensed counselor, I see people in these places all the time.
lines.zh: 身為一名持照的諮商師，我總是看到人們處於這樣的低谷。

lines.en: And as a human being living in this broken world, I've been in these places myself.
lines.zh: 而作為生活在這個破碎世界裡的一個人，我自己也曾經歷過這些低谷。

lines.en: What do we do when we're in the low places?
lines.zh: 當我們處於低谷時該怎麼辦？

lines.en: What do we do when the sadness seems like it might take over?
lines.zh: 當悲傷似乎快要將我們吞噬時，我們該怎麼辦？

lines.en: Well, what if, what if we did what the psalmist does?
lines.zh: 那麼，如果，如果我們照著詩人所做的去做呢？

lines.en: What does the psalmist do with his sadness?
lines.zh: 詩人如何處理他的悲傷？

lines.en: He laments it, he shares it and he entrusts it.
lines.zh: 他哀哭，他分享，並把它交託。

lines.en: Lament means to take all of the sadness, all the pain, all the doubt, all of it, and without holding back, pour it out in prayer.
lines.zh: 哀哭意味著帶著所有的悲傷、所有的痛苦、所有的懷疑，所有的一切，毫無保留地在禱告中傾吐出來。

lines.en: God, my soul, thirst for you.
lines.zh: 神啊，我的心切慕祢。

lines.en: My tears are my food.
lines.zh: 我的眼淚成為我的飲食。

lines.en: God, why have you forgotten me?
lines.zh: 神啊，祢為何忘記我？

lines.en: See how honest that is?
lines.zh: 看看那有多真實？

lines.en: But he not only laments his sorrow, he shares it.
lines.zh: 但他不僅為自己的悲哀哭泣，他還與人分享。

lines.en: The inscription says Psalm 42 is a psalm of the Sons of Cora.
lines.zh: 題注說詩篇第42篇是可拉後裔的訓誨詩。

lines.en: They were like a musical group.
lines.zh: 他們就像一個樂團一樣。

lines.en: You see, the writer of this psalm didn't sing alone.
lines.zh: 你看，這篇詩篇的作者不是獨自歌唱。

lines.en: He had friends who joined him in his sadness.
lines.zh: 他有朋友加入，與他分擔悲傷。

lines.en: My hope is that you have a friend to share in your sadness.
lines.zh: 我的盼望是，你也能有一位朋友來分擔你的悲傷。

lines.en: But then he entrusts it.
lines.zh: 但接著他將這一切交託。

lines.en: "Hope in God, O my soul," he says.
lines.zh: 他說：「我的心哪，應當仰望神。」

lines.en: When we're feeling this kind of lowness, we look to the one who came low for us.
lines.zh: 當我們感受到這種低谷時，我們要仰望那位為我們降卑的。

lines.en: Came as low as a torturous death on a cross.
lines.zh: 降卑到在十字架上受盡折磨而死的程度。

lines.en: Came low to secure our hope, that whatever we're going through today, there is a day coming when sadness will be gone forever.
lines.zh: 祂降卑是為了確保我們的盼望，也就是無論我們今天正在經歷什麼，終有一日，悲傷將永遠消失。

lines.en: And that day has been secured by Jesus.
lines.zh: 而那一天已經由耶穌為我們保證了。

lines.en: Hang in there.
lines.zh: 撐下去。

lines.en: Be honest with God because He is holding tightly to you.
lines.zh: 對神誠實，因為祂正緊緊地抓住你。

lessons.title: Are You a Courageous Person?
lessons.summaryZh: 勇敢不是沒有恐懼，而是帶著神同在的應許，即使害怕也繼續前進。

lines.en: I used to always wonder if people considered me a courageous person.
lines.zh: 我以前總是想知道，別人是否認為我是個勇敢的人。

lines.en: Most people probably wouldn't think themselves courageous.
lines.zh: 大多數人可能不會認為自己是勇敢的。

lines.en: We tend to reserve that title for others.
lines.zh: 我們往往把這個頭銜保留給別人。

lines.en: At least, I know I did.
lines.zh: 至少，我知道我以前是這樣。

lines.en: Me? Courageous? Maybe.
lines.zh: 我？勇敢？也許吧。

lines.en: But I could certainly point to more times in my life when I felt afraid than when I felt courageous.
lines.zh: 但我確實可以指出，在我生命中感到害怕的時刻，比感到勇敢的時刻還要多。

lines.en: I can think of moments in middle school where I was afraid to stand up for myself.
lines.zh: 我能想起在國中時，我害怕為自己挺身而出的時刻。

lines.en: Moments in college when I felt afraid to pursue full-time ministry because at the time my dad didn't approve.
lines.zh: 還有在大學時，因為當時我父親不贊成，我害怕追求全職服事的時刻。

lines.en: And even moments now in my adult life today where I'm afraid to mess up this whole parenting thing.
lines.zh: 甚至現在在我成年的生活中，我也會害怕把教養孩子這件事搞砸。

lines.en: I used to think having courage meant not being afraid, but I had it wrong.
lines.zh: 我以前認為有勇氣意味著不害怕，但我弄錯了。

lines.en: Having courage is not the absence of fear, but rather, having courage means moving forward even in the face of fear.
lines.zh: 有勇氣並非沒有恐懼，相反地，有勇氣意味著即使面對恐懼也能繼續前進。

lines.en: Courageous people do, in fact, feel fear, but they are compelled to push through their fear.
lines.zh: 勇敢的人事實上也會感到恐懼，但他們被驅使著去克服恐懼。

lines.en: That means you can't have courage without fear.
lines.zh: 那意味著如果沒有恐懼，你就無法擁有勇氣。

lines.en: Courageous people do it scared.
lines.zh: 勇敢的人是帶著恐懼去做的。

lines.en: One of my favorite characters in all of Scripture is a guy named Gideon.
lines.zh: 在整本聖經中，我最喜歡的人物之一是一個名叫基甸的人。

lines.en: And I think I like him so much because of how relatable he is.
lines.zh: 我想我這麼喜歡他，是因為他非常令人有共鳴。

lines.en: We are introduced to Gideon in the book of Judges during a time when Israel finds itself under the oppression of the Midianites.
lines.zh: 我們在士師記中認識了基甸，當時以色列正處於米甸人的壓迫之下。

lines.en: The odds were stacked against Israel.
lines.zh: 當時的局勢對以色列非常不利。

lines.en: They were constantly living in fear.
lines.zh: 他們一直生活在恐懼之中。

lines.en: And God has chosen Gideon to lead Israel into battle against them.
lines.zh: 神揀選了基甸帶領以色列人與他們爭戰。

lines.en: But Gideon is terrified.
lines.zh: 但基甸嚇壞了。

lines.en: He gives God all the valid reasons why he is not capable.
lines.zh: 他給了神所有合理的原因，說明他為什麼沒有能力。

lines.en: Honestly, you have to appreciate his self-awareness!
lines.zh: 老實說，你不得不欣賞他的自我認知！

lines.en: But God's response?
lines.zh: 但神的回答呢？

lines.en: Not empty affirmation.
lines.zh: 不是空洞的肯定。

lines.en: He knew what Gideon was and wasn't capable of.
lines.zh: 祂知道基甸能做什麼，不能做什麼。

lines.en: But God gave Gideon a promise that compelled Gideon to push through his fear and show courage.
lines.zh: 但神給了基甸一個應許，驅使基甸克服恐懼，展現勇氣。

lines.en: God promised Gideon, "I will be with you."
lines.zh: 神應許基甸：「我必與你同在。」

lines.en: And that truth rings true today.
lines.zh: 這個真理在今天依然適用。

lines.en: God is with you.
lines.zh: 神與你同在。

lines.en: God is with me.
lines.zh: 神與我同在。

lines.en: No matter what I face, no matter what I'm walking through, even when things aren't going the way my control-freak self had all planned out, or even when I'm down and hurting my God is still with me.
lines.zh: 無論我面對什麼，無論我正在經歷什麼，即使事情沒有按照我這個控制狂原本計畫的那樣發展，甚至當我低落和痛苦時，我的神依然與我同在。

lines.en: So I want to ask a question that could shake up your life in the best possible way: What would you do if you were confident that God was with you?
lines.zh: 所以我想問一個問題，它可能會以最好的方式改變你的人生：如果你深信神與你同在，你會怎麼做？

lines.en: For me the answer to that question has looked different during various seasons of my life.
lines.zh: 對我來說，這個問題的答案在我人生的不同階段中看起來是不一樣的。

lines.en: When I was in college it was standing up for my faith even when it cost me, and serving my church even when I felt unqualified.
lines.zh: 當我在大學時，它是即使要付出代價也要為我的信仰挺身而出，並且即使覺得自己不夠資格也要服事我的教會。

lines.en: More recently the answer to that question has looked like starting a college ministry and even navigating family drama and tension.
lines.zh: 最近，這個問題的答案看起來像是開始一個大學生事工，甚至是處理家庭的紛爭與緊張關係。

lines.en: What might it be for you?
lines.zh: 對你來說那會是什麼呢？

lines.en: What job would you accept or quit?
lines.zh: 你會接受或辭去什麼工作？

lines.en: What difficult conversation would you have?
lines.zh: 你會去進行什麼困難的對話？

lines.en: What conviction would you follow?
lines.zh: 你會去遵循什麼信念？

lines.en: What relationship would you seek to reconcile?
lines.zh: 你會尋求修復什麼樣的關係？

lines.en: God is with you, for you, behind you.
lines.zh: 神與你同在，支持你，在你身後。

lines.en: And while His presence is not a guarantee of an outcome that we would deem successful, one thing is for sure: we'll not regret courageously taking a step of faith God is calling us towards.
lines.zh: 雖然祂的同在並不能保證會有一個我們認為成功的結果，但有一件事是確定的：我們不會後悔勇敢地邁出神呼召我們踏出的信心步伐。

lines.en: So let's do it scared.
lines.zh: 所以，讓我們帶著恐懼去做吧。

lessons.title: Waiting to Bloom
lessons.summaryZh: 屬靈成長如同秋天播種，在看不見的暗處神正動工，時候到了必有收成。

lines.en: Planting bulbs in the fall feels almost irrational.
lines.zh: 在秋天種植球根感覺幾乎是不理智的。

lines.en: You bury something in the cold, hard soil, and then you just wait.
lines.zh: 你把東西埋在寒冷、堅硬的土壤裡，然後你只能等待。

lines.en: Months go by before you see anything.
lines.zh: 幾個月過去了，你才看到一點動靜。

lines.en: There's no color, no blooms.
lines.zh: 沒有顏色，沒有花朵。

lines.en: Just dirt and then snow.
lines.zh: 只有泥土，然後是雪。

lines.en: And then more dirt.
lines.zh: 然後是更多的泥土。

lines.en: But spring always tells the truth about what was planted.
lines.zh: 但是春天總是會說出關於種下了什麼的真相。

lines.en: We see in Galatians 6:7-9 that, "A man reaps what he sows.
lines.zh: 我們在加拉太書 6:7-9 中看到：「人種的是什麼，收的也是什麼。

lines.en: Whoever sows to please their flesh from the flesh will reap destruction.
lines.zh: 順著情慾撒種的，必從情慾收敗壞；

lines.en: Whoever sows to please the Spirit from the Spirit will reap eternal life.
lines.zh: 順著聖靈撒種的，必從聖靈收永生。

lines.en: Let us not become weary in doing good.
lines.zh: 我們行善，不可喪志；

lines.en: For at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up."
lines.zh: 若不灰心，到了時候就要收成。」

lines.en: Most spiritual growth feels like fall planting.
lines.zh: 大多數的屬靈成長感覺就像秋天的播種。

lines.en: You pray and don't see change yet.
lines.zh: 你禱告，卻還沒看到改變。

lines.en: You forgive, but the burden doesn't feel any lighter.
lines.zh: 你選擇饒恕，但重擔卻感覺沒有減輕。

lines.en: You choose obedience and it looks unimpressive, maybe even like the sacrifices have set you behind.
lines.zh: 你選擇順服，而這看起來並不顯眼，甚至可能覺得這些犧牲讓你落後了。

lines.en: But the hidden work matters and roots grow in dark places.
lines.zh: 但隱藏的工作很重要，根在黑暗的地方生長。

lines.en: If you're in a season that feels buried and not blooming, don't assume that nothing is happening.
lines.zh: 如果你正處在一個感覺被掩埋且沒有開花的季節，不要以為什麼事都沒發生。

lines.en: God does some of His most beautiful and substantial work in the underground places of our souls.
lines.zh: 神在我們靈魂深處，做了一些祂最美麗、最實質的工作。

lines.en: Spring takes time, and when the flowers finally arrive, the wait was well worth it.
lines.zh: 春天需要時間，而當花朵終於盛開時，這等待是非常值得的。

lessons.title: Do You Want to Be Healed?
lessons.summaryZh: 我們必須承認自己的破碎，放棄無效的自我醫治策略，將一切交給唯一的醫治者耶穌。

lines.en: In John chapter five, Jesus asks a question that at first glance seems puzzling, if not even offensive.
lines.zh: 在約翰福音第五章中，耶穌問了一個乍看之下令人不解，甚至有些冒犯的問題。

lines.en: He comes across a man who has been severely disabled for 38 years, and He asks him, “Do you want to be healed?”
lines.zh: 祂遇到一個重度殘疾三十八年的人，祂問他：「你要痊癒嗎？」

lines.en: Duh, what kind of question is that?
lines.zh: 廢話，這是什麼問題？

lines.en: Of course the man wants to be healed.
lines.zh: 這人當然想痊癒。

lines.en: The answer is obvious, but is it?
lines.zh: 答案顯而易見，但真的是這樣嗎？

lines.en: Is the answer so obvious?
lines.zh: 答案真的那麼明顯嗎？

lines.en: I've spent years as a pastor and a counselor, and in both of those roles, I found myself in situations where I've been sitting across from somebody else and I've had to ask them, do you really want to be healed?
lines.zh: 我當牧師和諮商師已經很多年了，在這兩個角色中，我常發現自己坐在某人對面，而我必須問他們，你真的想痊癒嗎？

lines.en: But do you know what else?
lines.zh: 但你知道嗎？

lines.en: I've not only asked that question of others, I've asked that question to myself.
lines.zh: 我不僅問過別人這個問題，我也問過自己。

lines.en: Joe, do you really want to be healed, to be changed, to be restored, to be made into the person you were created to be?
lines.zh: 喬，你真的想痊癒、被改變、被恢復，成為你受造時該有的樣子嗎？

lines.en: To put a fine point on this, I think many of us are actually afraid of healing, because healing means letting Jesus, even letting others into deep, dark, painful, ugly places.
lines.zh: 說白了，我認為我們很多人其實害怕得醫治，因為得醫治意味著讓耶穌，甚至讓別人進入我們內心深處那黑暗、痛苦、醜陋的地方。

vocab.form: To put a fine point on this

lines.en: And that's scary.
lines.zh: 而那是很可怕的。

lines.en: Healing means a completely new way of living in the fullness of what God has for us.
lines.zh: 得醫治意味著一種全新的生活方式，活在神為我們預備的豐盛中。

lines.en: And maybe, just maybe, if we're being honest, that new way of living sounds like more than we're ready for.
lines.zh: 也許，只要我們誠實面對自己，那種新的生活方式聽起來是我們還沒準備好要承受的。

lines.en: Like this man in John five, there are two things we have to accept, and these things are not exactly easy to accept.
lines.zh: 就像約翰福音第五章裡的這個人一樣，有兩件事我們必須接受，而這些事並不那麼容易接受。

lines.en: One, we've got to admit that we need healing.
lines.zh: 第一，我們必須承認我們需要醫治。

lines.en: Some of us still won't do that.
lines.zh: 我們有些人仍然不願意這麼做。

lines.en: I'll figure it out.
lines.zh: 我會自己想辦法的。

lines.en: I can fix my marriage.
lines.zh: 我能挽救我的婚姻。

lines.en: I'll quit this eventually.
lines.zh: 我最後一定會戒掉這個的。

lines.en: I just, I just have to try harder.
lines.zh: 我只是，我只是需要再努力一點。

lines.en: Are you willing to admit that there is deep brokenness in you?
lines.zh: 你願意承認你裡面有很深的破碎嗎？

lines.en: Are you willing to admit you're as desperate for healing as this man in John five?
lines.zh: 你願意承認你和約翰福音第五章這個人一樣，極度渴望得到醫治嗎？

lines.en: And two, we have to admit our strategies to heal ourselves don't work.
lines.zh: 第二，我們必須承認我們自我醫治的策略是無效的。

lines.en: This man was trying to get healed by taking a dip in a pool, but that obviously hadn't worked for 38 years.
lines.zh: 這人試圖藉由在池子裡泡一下來得醫治，但這在三十八年來顯然沒有奏效。

lines.en: We too have our own failed healing strategies.
lines.zh: 我們也有自己失敗的醫治策略。

lines.en: When we try to find healing and success and approval and pleasure and a hundred other things that do nothing to bring true and lasting healing.
lines.zh: 當我們試圖尋找醫治、成功、認同和享樂，以及其他一百種對帶來真實和持久醫治毫無幫助的事物時。

lines.en: Jesus is asking us, are we willing to turn from our sad strategies and trust Him instead?
lines.zh: 耶穌在問我們，我們是否願意轉離我們可悲的策略，轉而信靠祂？

lines.en: So do you want to be healed?
lines.zh: 所以，你要痊癒嗎？

lines.en: If so, bring it all to Jesus and invite Him to do it only He can do.
lines.zh: 如果是的話，把這一切都帶到耶穌面前，邀請祂成就只有祂能做的事。

lines.en: It might look different than you think.
lines.zh: 過程可能跟你想的不一樣。

lines.en: He may want to use people in your life to deliver His care.
lines.zh: 祂可能想透過你生命中的人來傳遞祂的關懷。

lines.en: It might take longer than you think.
lines.zh: 這可能需要比你想像更長的時間。

lines.en: Full and complete healing may not be on this side of heaven, but He is the only healer.
lines.zh: 在回天家之前，可能無法得到完全徹底的醫治，但祂是唯一的醫治者。

lines.en: Go to Him today.
lines.zh: 今天就到祂那裡去吧。

lessons.title: Why Are You So Afraid?
lessons.summaryZh: 當信心增長，恐懼就縮小；耶穌能平息罪惡與我們生命中的任何風暴。

lines.en: As we study the Bible, we learn that the size of our faith impacts the size of our fear.
lines.zh: 當我們研讀聖經時，我們學到信心的大小會影響我們恐懼的多寡。

lines.en: As faith grows, fear shrinks.
lines.zh: 當信心增長，恐懼就縮小。

lines.en: In Mark chapter four, Jesus and his followers are on a boat and a storm blows through that was wild enough to scare these veterans of the sea.
lines.zh: 在馬可福音第四章中，耶穌和跟隨祂的人在一艘船上，突然颳起了一陣風暴，猛烈到足以嚇壞這些海上老手。

lines.en: They wake up a sleeping Jesus and question Him, asking, “Don't you even care that we're about to drown?”
lines.zh: 他們叫醒沉睡的耶穌並質問祂，問道：「我們喪命，你不顧嗎？」

lines.en: You ever felt that way?
lines.zh: 你曾有過那種感覺嗎？

lines.en: Ever felt like maybe God was unconcerned that your life was or is falling apart?
lines.zh: 是否曾覺得神似乎不在乎你的生活正分崩離析？

lines.en: The cancer's back.
lines.zh: 癌症復發了。

lines.en: The marriage is in shambles.
lines.zh: 婚姻一塌糊塗。

lines.en: The kids are struggling.
lines.zh: 孩子們正在掙扎。

lines.en: The finances are a disaster.
lines.zh: 財務狀況是一場災難。

lines.en: The loneliness is overwhelming, and God feels, well, asleep.
lines.zh: 孤獨感令人窒息，而神感覺起來，嗯，卻在沉睡。

lines.en: In the story, Jesus wakes up and tells the wind to calm down.
lines.zh: 在故事中，耶穌醒來並吩咐風平靜下來。

lines.en: And it does.
lines.zh: 風就止住了。

lines.en: Then Jesus asks a really important question.
lines.zh: 然後耶穌問了一個非常重要的問題。

lines.en: A question that would be good for you and me to consider in the middle of our storms.
lines.zh: 這是一個值得你我在風暴中思考的好問題。

lines.en: He asks, “Why are you so afraid?
lines.zh: 祂問：「為什麼膽怯？

lines.en: Do you still have no faith?”
lines.zh: 你們還沒有信心嗎？」

lines.en: See, that storm wasn't even a big one.
lines.zh: 你看，那場風暴甚至不算大。

lines.en: Jesus was about to calm the greatest storm the world had ever known.
lines.zh: 耶穌即將平息世界上前所未見的最大風暴。

lines.en: The cyclone of sin that rages in our lives.
lines.zh: 就是在我們生命中肆虐的罪惡狂風。

lines.en: And if He can calm that storm, what could we possibly be afraid of?
lines.zh: 如果祂能平息那場風暴，我們還有什麼好怕的呢？

lines.en: So what about you?
lines.zh: 那麼你呢？

lines.en: Are you living in fear today?
lines.zh: 你今天活在恐懼中嗎？

lines.en: Are you stuck in a storm that has you freaking out?
lines.zh: 你是否困在讓你嚇壞了的風暴中？

lines.en: Jesus, who has the power to calm your storm, would say to you, “Come on, why are you so afraid?
lines.zh: 有能力平息你的風暴的耶穌會對你說：「來吧，為什麼膽怯？

lines.en: Do you still have no faith?
lines.zh: 你還沒有信心嗎？

lines.en: I stopped sin.
lines.zh: 我已經阻止了罪惡。

lines.en: There is no storm I can't handle.”
lines.zh: 沒有我處理不了的風暴。」

lines.en: So cry out to Him today and tell Him, “I believe you can calm my storm.
lines.zh: 所以今天向祂呼求，並告訴祂：「我相信祢能平息我的風暴。

lines.en: And I trust in you.”
lines.zh: 我信靠祢。」

lines.en: Do it now.
lines.zh: 現在就做吧。

lines.en: Click pause, look up.
lines.zh: 按下暫停鍵，抬頭仰望。

lines.en: Tell Him you know He's got you.
lines.zh: 告訴祂你知道祂會看顧你。

lessons.title: Wait on God
lessons.summaryZh: 與其靠自己盲目衝撞，不如耐心等候神，因為我們真正的盼望在於祂。

lines.en: My kids used to love the movie "Homeward Bound."
lines.zh: 我的孩子們以前很喜歡看電影《返家十萬里》。

lines.en: It's pretty great.
lines.zh: 這是一部很棒的電影。

lines.en: Two dogs and a cat, they try to make their way across a mountain range to get back to their families.
lines.zh: 兩隻狗和一隻貓，牠們試圖越過山脈，回到家人身邊。

lines.en: It's a fun one.
lines.zh: 這是一部很有趣的電影。

lines.en: It wasn't until, like, the 10th time watching this movie with my kids that I realized all of this could have been avoided if they had just waited.
lines.zh: 直到我陪孩子們看了大概十次這部電影之後，我才意識到，如果牠們乖乖等待，這一切本來是可以避免的。

lines.en: The owners were coming back for them in a couple of days.
lines.zh: 主人幾天後就會回來接牠們。

lines.en: Sure, it was an adventure, but two of them nearly died along the way.
lines.zh: 當然，這是一場冒險，但其中兩隻幾乎在途中喪命。

lines.en: All they had to do was wait.
lines.zh: 牠們所要做的就只是等待。

lines.en: We to get ourselves into trouble when instead of waiting on God, we try and take matters into our own hands and we rush forward without Him.
lines.zh: 當我們不等候神，反而試圖自己掌控局面，並在沒有祂的情況下向前衝時，我們也會讓自己陷入麻煩。

vocab.form: take matters into our own hands
vocab.lemma: take matters into one's own hands

lines.en: In Psalm 62, David writes a poem from the perspective of somebody under attack, and he tells himself in verse five, "For God alone, O my soul, wait in silence, for my hope is from Him."
lines.zh: 在詩篇62篇中，大衛從一個受到攻擊之人的角度寫了一首詩，他在第五節對自己說：「我的心哪，你當默默無聲，專等候神，因為我的盼望是從祂而來。」

lines.en: I love how he has to tell this to himself, "Soul, don't rush forward in your own strength.
lines.zh: 我很喜歡他必須這樣對自己說：「我的心，不要靠著自己的力量向前衝。

lines.en: Wait on God.
lines.zh: 要等候神。

lines.en: That's where your true hope is."
lines.zh: 那是你真正盼望的所在。」

lines.en: Do you feel like you're waiting on God?
lines.zh: 你覺得自己正在等候神嗎？

lines.en: For a job, for a kid, for a kid to come back, for a marriage miracle.
lines.zh: 為了工作、為了孩子、為了孩子回家、為了一次婚姻的奇蹟。

lines.en: For a treatment to take.
lines.zh: 為了治療能見效。

lines.en: For an addiction to heal?
lines.zh: 為了成癮能被治癒？

lines.en: I hate waiting as much as you do, as much as David did, as much as those two dogs and that cat.
lines.zh: 我和你一樣討厭等待，就像大衛一樣，也像那兩隻狗和那隻貓一樣。

lines.en: But better to wait on Him than rush forward without Him.
lines.zh: 但等候祂總比沒有祂而向前衝來得好。

lines.en: Go to Him today.
lines.zh: 今天就到祂那裡去吧。

lines.en: And in addition to asking Him to end the waiting.
lines.zh: 除了求祂結束這等待之外。

lines.en: Thank Him for being near to you in the waiting, and ask Him to show you what He's doing in you, in the midst of the waiting.
lines.zh: 也要感謝祂在等待中與你親近，並求祂向你顯明，在這等待的過程中，祂正在你裡面做什麼。

lessons.title: Walk in the Light
lessons.summaryZh: 耶穌是世界的光，當我們降服並跟從祂，就能走出黑暗，得著全新的生命。

lines.en: You ever felt lost in life?
lines.zh: 你曾對人生感到迷惘嗎？

lines.en: Kind of like trying to navigate a dark room, walking around aimlessly, unsure of your next step.
lines.zh: 就像試著在暗房裡摸索，漫無目的地走著，不知道下一步該往哪裡走。

lines.en: It's unsettling, disorienting, and even stressful.
lines.zh: 這令人不安、失去方向，甚至感到備受壓力。

lines.en: After their escape from Egypt, the people of Israel were lost and wandered in the wilderness for forty years.
lines.zh: 以色列人逃離埃及後，迷失了方向，在曠野飄流了四十年。

lines.en: But God sent a pillar of cloud that would guide them by day and it would turn to fire to guide them by night.
lines.zh: 但神差遣雲柱在白晝引導他們，到了夜間則變成火柱來引導他們。

lines.en: God’s faithfulness to guide them is celebrated in the Feast of Tabernacles.
lines.zh: 住棚節就是在慶祝神引導他們的信實。

lines.en: And a major component of the Feast of Tabernacles was the lighting of big lamps in the temple courts.
lines.zh: 而住棚節的一個主要環節，就是在聖殿的院子裡點燃大燈。

lines.en: The lights were a reminder of God guiding them by night.
lines.zh: 這些燈光提醒著他們神在夜間的引導。

lines.en: And it is within that context, during the Feast of Tabernacles, that Jesus made this powerful statement:
lines.zh: 正是在那樣的背景下，在住棚節期間，耶穌作出了這個強而有力的宣告：

lines.en: “I am the light of the world.
lines.zh: 「我是世界的光。

lines.en: Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness but will have the light of life.”
lines.zh: 跟從我的，就不在黑暗裡走，必要得著生命的光。」

lines.en: What a moment!
lines.zh: 這是何等重要的一刻！

lines.en: Jesus was saying, “I know God sent your ancestors a light to guide them before but now he’s sent the light of the world to lead you into salvation now.”
lines.zh: 耶穌的意思是：「我知道神過去曾賜給你們祖先光來引導他們，但現在祂差遣了世界的光，要在此刻引領你們進入救恩。」

lines.en: When we surrender to and follow Jesus, we’ll never walk in the disorienting darkness because Jesus illuminates for us a new life.
lines.zh: 當我們降服並跟從耶穌時，我們就再也不會走在令人迷失的黑暗中，因為耶穌為我們照亮了新生命。

lines.en: Jesus, the light of the world, came to be the light of your world.
lines.zh: 耶穌，這世界的光，來作你生命世界的光。

lines.en: So be encouraged today that the light of Jesus dispels the darkness of fear, shame, brokenness, sin, and death with the light of peace, purpose, forgiveness, restoration, hope, and grace.
lines.zh: 所以今天願你得著鼓勵，耶穌的光用平安、目標、饒恕、恢復、盼望和恩典的光，驅散了恐懼、羞恥、破碎、罪惡與死亡的黑暗。

lessons.title: Trusting God in Our Work
lessons.summaryZh: 求神帶領工作中的會議，賜下智慧和清晰的異象，並在一切事上榮耀祂。

lines.en: God, I pray over this meeting I have coming up.
lines.zh: 神啊，我為這場即將到來的會議禱告。

lines.en: Thank you in advance that you are already on the other side of these conversations, and for leading our team in the direction we should go in.
lines.zh: 預先感謝祢，因為祢已經在這些對話的另一端，並帶領我們的團隊走在我們該走的方向上。

lines.en: Help us to ask the questions you want to answer and tune our ears to hear your voice.
lines.zh: 幫助我們問出祢想回答的問題，並調整我們的耳朵來聽祢的聲音。

lines.en: Empower us through your Spirit to communicate our thoughts and ideas effectively and kindly.
lines.zh: 藉著祢的靈賦予我們能力，使我們能有效且友善地溝通我們的想法和點子。

lines.en: Teach us to be quick to listen and slow to defensiveness.
lines.zh: 教導我們快快地聽，慢慢地起防衛心。

lines.en: I ask for a clear vision and a way forward, and I believe that your word is a lamp to our feet and a light to our path.
lines.zh: 我求一個清晰的異象和前進的道路，並且我相信祢的話是我們腳前的燈，是我們路上的光。

lines.en: May our team continue to honor and glorify you in all we do.
lines.zh: 願我們的團隊在我們所做的一切事上繼續尊榮並榮耀祢。

lines.en: We love you and thank you for trusting us with this work.
lines.zh: 我們愛祢，並感謝祢將這份工作託付給我們。

lines.en: Amen.
lines.zh: 阿們。

lessons.title: The Good Samaritan
lessons.summaryZh: 耶穌透過好撒馬利亞人的比喻，教導我們何謂真正的愛鄰舍如同自己。

lines.en: Now I want you to turn with me tonight to the 10th chapter of Luke.
lines.zh: 今晚我要你們和我一起翻到《路加福音》第十章。

lines.en: A very familiar passage that every young person here will relate to; young and old.
lines.zh: 這是一段非常熟悉的經文，在座的每位年輕人都能產生共鳴，無論老少。

lines.en: The 10th chapter of Luke, beginning at the 25th verse,
lines.zh: 《路加福音》第十章，從第25節開始：

lines.en: "And behold, a certain lawyer stood up and tempted him,
lines.zh: 「有一個律法師起來試探耶穌，

lines.en: saying, Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?"
lines.zh: 說：『夫子！我該做甚麼才可以承受永生？』」

lines.en: Now Jesus was asked that same question about 19 times in his period of ministry that is recorded in the Gospels.
lines.zh: 在四福音書記載的服事期間，耶穌大約被問過19次同樣的問題。

lines.en: In various forms he was asked that question.
lines.zh: 人們以各種不同的形式問祂這個問題。

lines.en: "What must I do to inherit eternal life?"
lines.zh: 「我該做甚麼才可以承受永生？」

lines.en: And he said unto him, "What is written in the law?
lines.zh: 耶穌對他說：「律法上寫的是甚麼？

lines.en: How readest thou?"
lines.zh: 你念的是怎樣呢？」

lines.en: And he answering said, "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, with all thy soul, with all thy strength,
lines.zh: 他回答說：「你要盡心、盡性、盡力、

lines.en: and with all thy mind; and thy neighbor as thyself."
lines.zh: 盡意愛主─你的神；又要愛鄰舍如同自己。」

lines.en: And he said unto him, "Thou hast answered right:
lines.zh: 耶穌說：「你回答的是；

lines.en: this do, and thou shalt live."
lines.zh: 你這樣行，就必得存活。」

lines.en: But no one has ever done it.
lines.zh: 但從來沒有人做到過。

lines.en: No one in the history of the human race has ever loved God with all his heart, mind, and strength all of his life,
lines.zh: 在人類歷史上，從未有人一生都盡心、盡意、盡力愛神，

lines.en: and his neighbor as himself all his life.
lines.zh: 也從未有人一生都愛鄰舍如同自己。

lines.en: That's the reason we've all come short, we're all sinners,
lines.zh: 這就是為什麼我們都有所虧欠，我們都是罪人，

lines.en: and we all need to repent of our sins, and find forgiveness at the cross.
lines.zh: 我們都需要為自己的罪悔改，並在十字架前尋求赦免。

lines.en: But he, willing still now to justify himself, (as many of you would like to justify yourselves)
lines.zh: 但那人現在仍要顯明自己有理（就像你們許多人也喜歡為自己辯護一樣），

lines.en: said, "But who is my neighbor?"
lines.zh: 就對耶穌說：「誰是我的鄰舍呢？」

lines.en: See, he was a lawyer and it was his job to cross-examine.
lines.zh: 看吧，他是一名律法師，他的工作就是盤問。
